message.content:
Read-only analysis. Change nothing — do not edit any file.

Three documents were rewritten as a full revision (de-duplicating and restructuring). I need to
know whether anything VALUABLE was lost.

Compare each new version against its backup:

| new | backup |
|---|---|
| /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/fedLead-playbook.md (688 lines) | /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/jobs/652997c6/tmp/fedLead-playbook.backup.md (800 lines) |
| /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/fedBuild-manual.md (685 lines) | /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/jobs/652997c6/tmp/fedBuild-manual.backup.md (1056 lines) |
| /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/uiBuild-knowledge.md (690 lines) | /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/jobs/652997c6/tmp/uiBuild-knowledge.backup.md (456 lines) |

Also check whether anything valuable from the RETIRED document was dropped without being
migrated: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/jobs/652997c6/tmp/zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.backup.md
(474 lines). Its principles were supposed to move into fedLead-playbook.md sections 3 and 4.

`fedBuild-manual.md` shrank the most (1056 → 685). That's the highest-risk file for accidental
loss. Prioritise it.

For each document, report:

1. **Substantive content present in the backup and ABSENT from the new version.** Ignore pure
   restructuring, rewording, and deliberate de-duplication (the same fact stated in two
   documents, now stated in one). I want facts, worked examples, code snippets, tables,
   warnings, or specific numbers that are simply GONE and not restated anywhere across the
   three new documents. Check all three new files before declaring something lost — content may
   have moved between documents.

2. For each loss, judge: **WORTH RESTORING** or **CORRECTLY DROPPED**. Correctly dropped = it
   was duplicated elsewhere, it was training material for a different stack, it was superseded
   by a correction, or it was a stale claim. Give your reasoning in one line.

3. **Anything in the new versions that contradicts something else in the new versions.** Check
   across all three files, not just within one.

4. **Voice/register drift** — the backups had distinct registers (fedLead: terse, table-first;
   fedBuild: instructional second-person, code-heavy; uiBuild: near-impersonal, bold-lead-in +
   declarative). Note any section in the new versions that noticeably breaks its document's
   established voice.

Be specific and quote the missing passage. Rank losses by how much they'd cost someone who
needed that fact and couldn't find it. Do not suggest rewrites — this is an audit.

    11	---
    12	
    13	## 1. The Operating Principles
    14	
    15	Four things were agreed that change how you build. They apply to every story.
    16	
    17	### Static-first
    18	
    19	Where an integration isn't available yet, **build against static data and move on.** Do not block, and
    20	do not stub out a fake integration layer.
    21	
    22	- Props in, markup out. The component takes the data it renders as props.
    23	- Static/mock data lives in the **story**, not in the component.
    24	- No data-fetching hooks inside `overrides/app/components/` — that's the container/presentational rule
    25	  in `.claude/rules/components.md`, and it's what makes the later wiring a one-file change instead of
    26	  a rewrite.
    27	
    28	When Contentful (or SFCC, or Omneo) comes online, the component doesn't change — the page or container
    29	that feeds it does. If you find yourself writing "temporary" fetch logic inside a component, stop:
    30	that's the thing static-first exists to prevent.
    31	
    32	### Leverage what exists before building
    33	
    34	In priority order — this is the ladder, and you should be able to say which rung you landed on:
    35	
    36	```
    37	Salesforce / PWA Kit base capability
    38	        ↓  nothing fits
    39	Existing shared component in overrides/
    40	        ↓  nothing fits
    41	Existing pattern in the codebase
    42	        ↓  nothing fits
    43	New implementation  ← justify this in the PR description
    44	```
    45	
    46	F2R outputs count as "existing": the onshore design team's outputs, Jersey's work (currently mostly
    47	primitive/foundation-level), and the design foundations now in the codebase. Use them where they fit
    48	rather than starting clean.
    49	
    50	**The default is override, not build.** Not for tidiness — because an override **inherits the wiring for
    51	free.** Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart
    52	modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of
    53	those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed — none of which is visible in the story points, and
    54	all of which lands on you.
    55	
    56	There's a second effect worth understanding, because it changes where your work shows up. PWA Kit's
    57	resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
    58	already import means the entire base template inherits your version** — zero call sites touched. A
    59	bespoke component in a new folder only reaches the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same result
    60	on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site.
    61	
    62	⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel
    63	(`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from
    64	'./Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
    65	specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import
    66	that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>/` intercepts
    67	nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not
    68	an interception point. See "Two component families" below.
    69	
    70	If you do land on "build custom", expect to justify it in the PR — that's not a formality, it's the one
    71	question review will always ask.
    72	
    73	### Figma stays open the whole time
    74	
    75	Figma is not a one-time handoff you read and close. Keep it open and use it to actively find problems:
    76	
    77	- Validate the build against the design as you go, not at the end.
    78	- Spot **missing tokens** — a value in Figma with no counterpart in `theme/foundation/`.
    79	- Spot **missing design definitions** — a state (hover, disabled, error, empty) with no design.
    80	- Catch discrepancies between design and implementation.
    81	
    82	When you find a gap, **raise it** — §7 covers where it goes. Silently inventing a value is the failure
    83	mode; a hardcoded hex that "looked right" is how a design system dies.
    84	
    85	**Check the Figma link on the card actually points at your story's frame.** Because we work through the
    86	Figma MCP, that link isn't a reference — it's effectively the spec, and whatever it points at is what
    87	gets built.
    88	
    89	A wrong or stale link doesn't announce itself. It produces a component built to the wrong design, AC
    90	signed off against a different frame, and QA testing a third source — none of which surfaces until page
    91	assembly. If the link looks wrong, **ask the BA (Jas) to fix the card**, don't just work it out in a DM.
    92	A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — which the BA and QA both read —
    93	still wrong.
    94	
    95	### Ask in the group chat
    96	
    97	Work it out together rather than solo. If you've been stuck more than ~30 minutes, or you're about to
    98	make a decision that affects more than your own component, post it. These threads are how the team
    99	learns as a group — a question you think is basic is usually three people's question.
   100	
   101	Claude is part of the workflow where it fits. Treat its output the way you'd treat a colleague's
   102	first draft: useful, and checked before it ships.
   103	
   104	### The bar you're building to
   105	
   106	Worth knowing, because it explains why review here is stricter than you may be used to:
   107	**the SOW allows no more than 10 defects across the build, and no Sev3.**
   108	
   109	Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination removes the usual
   110	"ship it, fix it in QA" option — a visual defect that would be a shrug elsewhere consumes part of a very
   111	small budget. Practically, for you:
   112	
   113	- Expect UI PRs to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma, not just the diff.
   114	- Self-review the same way before you open it (§8). It's faster than a review round-trip.
   115	- Where design is missing or contradictory, **flag it** rather than picking something plausible. An
   116	  invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence — two problems instead of none.
   117	
   118	---
   119	
   120	## 2. Before you write any code
   121	
   122	Five minutes here saves a day later.
   123	
   124	### Run the session start
   125	
   126	```bash
   127	/session-start
   128	```
   129	
   130	Reads the tracking docs, checks your branch, states where the project is. Do it once per session.
   131	
   132	### Confirm your branch
   133	
   134	```bash
   135	git branch --show-current
   136	```
   137	
   138	`feature/*` or `fix/*`, branched from `develop`. **If it says `develop` or `main`, stop.** No exceptions.
   139	
   140	### Check what already exists
   141	
   142	| Question | Where to look |
   143	|---|---|
   144	| Does a Base / Override / Custom component already cover this? | `.claude/registry/components.md` |
   145	| Same for hooks, utils, pages, routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
   146	| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` |
   147	| Which tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier <path>` |
   148	| Is another squad the owner? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squad{A,B}.md` |
   149	
   150	The registry's **`Origin`** column is the one that matters most:
   151	
   152	- **`Custom`** — a Zimmermann component already in `overrides/`. Extend it.
   153	- **`Override`** — a base component already scaffolded into `overrides/`. Edit it directly.
   154	- **`Base`** — it exists upstream but is **not** in `overrides/` yet. **This has a cost.** See below.
   155	
   156	### Three component families — and they do different jobs
   157	
   158	`overrides/app/components/` holds three kinds of thing. Knowing which you're writing decides the path, the
   159	naming, and whether it affects anything but your own page.
   160	
   161	| | `components/<kebab-name>/` | `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules}/<camelName>/` | `components/shared/ui/<PascalName>/` |
   162	|---|---|---|---|
   163	| **What it is** | An override of an SFCC component | A Zimmermann design-system component | A raw primitive — Link, Text, Image, Button |
   164	| **Naming** | Keep SFCC's kebab-case exactly (`product-tile/`) | **camelCase** (`zimmButton/`) | Mirror upstream's PascalCase (`Button/`) |
   165	| **Layout** | `index.tsx` + story | `index.tsx` + story, one folder per component | `index.tsx` |
   166	| **Intercepts SFCC?** | **Yes** — base files import by full package path | No | **No** — see the barrel exception above |
   167	| **Who consumes it** | Every base page that used it, plus you | Our own pages and components | Explicit importers — chiefly Contentful renderers |
   168	| **Reach for it when** | Changing how an SFCC component looks or behaves | Building a Zimmermann component from the F2R design library | You want a plain branded primitive, no commerce semantics |
   169	
   170	The `shared/ui` family exists because **Contentful renderers need primitives, not commerce components.**
   171	Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection` (`Box`, `Text`),
   172	`collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup` (`Box`, `Image`, `Link`, `Skeleton`,
   173	`Text`), `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `shoppableImage`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra
   174	(`shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`). A CMS rich-text
   175	renderer mapping a `hyperlink` node to a `Link` wants exactly that — predictable and unopinionated — not a
   176	component carrying SFCC's locale-routing and commerce behaviour.
   177	
   178	**Status: the intent is agreed, the wiring is not built.** A `shared/ui/Button` exists on
   179	`feature/pdp-token-class-spike`, its only consumer is the `/dev/components` catalogue page, there is no
   180	`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx` barrel, and `collectionHero` still imports `Button` from
   181	the SFCC barrel — so it still gets raw Chakra. Don't build against this family until the barrel question
   182	is settled (see the playbook).
   183	
   184	### Atoms and molecules — where they go and what they're called
   185	
   186	**Decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live under:
   187	
   188	```
   189	overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
   190	  atoms/       zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
   191	  molecules/   zimmInputAction/
   192	  organisms/   (when the first one lands)
   193	               └── index.tsx  +  index.stories.tsx
   194	```
   195	
   196	**Naming is `camelCase`, one folder per component, `index.tsx` inside.** That follows
   197	`conventions.md` — these are Zimmermann-authored, so camelCase; the kebab-case rule applies *only* to files
   198	mirroring a base Salesforce file, and there is no `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` to mirror. It also satisfies
   199	`components.md`'s rule that **the named export matches the folder name** — `zimmButton/` exports
   200	`ZimmButton`. Precedents already in the repo: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`.
   201	
   202	Three casings exist and each is correct in its own family — don't generalise from one to another:
   203	
   204	| Family | Casing | Why |
   205	|---|---|---|
   206	| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Must match upstream; their files import that path |
   207	| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | **Zimmermann-authored — the default rule** |
   208	| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own PascalCase exactly |
   209	
   210	**Which tier?** Atom / molecule / organism is decided by **what the component's own template renders**,
   211	not by how big it looks:
   212	
   213	- **Atom** — renders no other component. Markup, CSS and tokens only.
   214	- **Molecule** — renders only atoms.
   215	- **Organism** — renders at least one molecule.
   216	
   217	Two rules that settle most arguments: **an icon passed as a prop doesn't count** (`icon="close"` keeps a
   218	Button an atom), and **slotted children don't count** — only what your own template renders. A top bar
   219	composing just Button + Logo is a molecule even though it spans the viewport; tier follows composition,
   220	not pixel size.
   221	
   222	If you're porting from the F2R design library, the tier is already recorded there as `composes: [...]` —
   223	use it rather than re-deriving. Add a `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` line in the JSDoc so
   224	the link back to the contract survives.
   225	
   226	### What's actually overridden today
   227	
   228	Worth knowing before you estimate anything: **`overrides/app/components/` currently contains seven
   229	directories.** As of `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`:
   230	
   231	```
   232	_app-config   button   contentful   foundation   header   icons   pageContainer
   233	```
   234	
   235	That's it. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
   236	`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`** — they exist upstream and are
   237	referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` and the protected-file lists, but they have **not** been scaffolded
   238	into `overrides/` yet.
   239	
   240	Two consequences:
   241	
   242	- **Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first** (below). Assume it until the registry says otherwise.
   243	- **When a rules file points at one of those as an example, the file won't be there.** The convention is
   244	  real; the worked example often isn't yet. Check before you go looking.
   245	
   246	### If `Origin = Base`, the copy-first rule applies
   247	
   248	Before any functional work, AGENTS.md requires:
   249	
   250	1. Copy the base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` (keep the kebab-case filename exactly)
   251	2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports
   252	3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
   253	4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` marker
   254	5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override is rendering instead of the base
   255	6. Then build; remove the markers
   256	
   257	It's serialised and human-gated, and **the first story against a given base component pays it — later
   258	ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement,
   259	not on day three of the sprint.
   260	
   261	### Sanity-check the scope
   262	
   263	```bash
   264	/scope-check
   265	```
   266	
   267	Classifies everything you're about to touch by tier and tells you if the change is safe, risky, or
   268	blocked. Worth it any time you're not certain.
   269	
   270	---
   271	
   272	## 3. Design Foundations — read this before your first component
   273	
   274	**Canonical reference: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`.** That file is the authority on styling an
   275	override; this section is the orientation for it. If the two ever disagree, the rules file wins — and
   276	this section needs a fix, so raise it.
   277	
   278	The design system lives in `overrides/app/theme/`. It has **one** source of truth and derives outward:
   279	
   280	```
   281	foundation/  colour.ts · typography.ts · spacing.ts · sizes.ts · motion.ts · gridSystem.ts
   282	        |  imported and derived from — never retyped
   283	foundation/zimmTokens.ts          -> the --zimm-* CSS custom properties
   284	        |  consumed by
   285	theme/components/*.ts (recipes)   ·   globalStyles.ts (.zimm-* classes)
   286	```
   287	
   288	`zimmTokens.ts` is **derived**, not a second copy — it imports `colors.grey[900]` rather than retyping
   289	`#191919`. That is why you never edit it directly, and why two values cannot drift apart.
   290	`theme/index.test.tsx` guards the arrangement with 125 tests; a failure there is a real drift signal,
   291	not test noise.
   292	
   293	### The styling hierarchy — reach for these in order
   294	
   295	This is the load-bearing rule of the whole section.
   296	
   297	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`
   298	2. **Semantic token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   299	   `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`
   300	3. **The component's own `theme/components/<name>.ts`** for anything that varies by variant / size /
   301	   state. For an interactive component with Chakra support (buttons, inputs, links) that file is the
   302	   **single source of truth**
   303	4. **`sx` prop** for a genuine one-off gap in the Chakra prop system
   304	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` truly cannot express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes)
   305	
   306	**Never** a raw hex / px / rem / em literal in a component file. The one standing exception is
   307	`button.ts`'s provisional constants — trap 2 below.
   308	
   309	Registered component recipes today: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` (`theme/components/index.ts`).
   310	Adding a new one is yours to do — one file per Chakra component, registered in that index.
   311	
   312	### Setting type — always `textStyle`, never `fontSize`
   313	
   314	```tsx
   315	<Text textStyle="body1">…</Text>          // ✅
   316	<Heading textStyle="heading3">…</Heading>  // ✅
   317	<Text fontSize="md">…</Text>               // ❌ never
   318	```
   319	
   320	**Why this is a hard rule, not a preference.** Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra
   321	defaults, and the base retail-react-app uses those names at ~199 call sites:
   322	
   323	| Key | Zimmermann | Chakra |
   324	|---|---|---|
   325	| `md` | 24px | 16px |
   326	| `xs` | 16px | 12px |
   327	| `2xs` | 14px | 10px |
   328	| `3xs` | 12px | 7.2px |
   329	
   330	The Zimmermann font scale is **deliberately not registered** as `theme.fontSizes` for exactly this
   331	reason. If you write `fontSize="md"` expecting 24px you get 16px. If you "fix" that by registering the
   332	scale, you silently restyle every base component on the site. There's a test guarding against it —
   333	don't fight it, use `textStyle`.
   334	
   335	**The 22 available text styles:**
   336	
   337	`heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` ·
   338	`mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` ·
   339	`button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`
   340	
   341	Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation → Typography**.
   342	
   343	### Colour — use the semantic aliases
   344	
   345	```tsx
   346	<Box bg="background.01" color="text.default" borderColor="border.default" />   // ✅
   347	<Box bg="#f9f8f6" color="#191919" />                                          // ❌
   348	```
   349	
   350	Two layers exist. Reach for the **semantic** layer; the primitives are what the semantics are built from.
   351	
   352	| Group | Keys |
   353	|---|---|
   354	| `text.*` | `default` `inverse` `inverseGrey` `secondary` `muted` |
   355	| `background.*` | `01`–`07` (`01`–`04` light/ivory, `05`–`06` dark, `07` white) |
   356	| `border.*` | `default` `secondary` `focus` `forms` `error` |
   357	| `status.*` | `success` `error` `errorBackground` `storeClosed` |
   358	| `link.*` · `icon.*` | `default` `hover` · `default` |
   359	| `action.primary.*` | `bgDefault` `bgHover` `bgPressed` `bgDisabled` `bgFocused` `text` `textDisabled` |
   360	| `action.secondary.*` | `border` `bgHover` `text` `textInverse` `textDisabled` |
   361	| Primitives | `grey.{black,900,800,700,600,500,300,200,100,white}` `ivory.{100..400}` `coral/green/orange/red.500` `opacity.{15,30,40,50}` |
   362	
   363	Browse under **Foundation → Colour**.
   364	
   365	### Spacing
   366	
   367	Both scales work — Chakra's numerics are preserved and the Zimmermann named scale is added on top.

   373	```

   377	the default 16px root font-size.

   380	zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). Hairline geometry deliberately does not:

   392	something to reference. The named scale is the Chakra-facing surface:

   400	and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64) — that's a **token gap to raise** (§7), not a reason to reach
   401	for the numeric alias.

   404	
   405	These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere),
   406	so they're **imported as constants** instead:

   408	```tsx
   409	import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';
   410	
   411	<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                                    // 20px
   412	<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />                          // 52px
   413	transition: `opacity ${motion.duration.fast} ${motion.easing.standard}`
   414	```

   416	`iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
   417	`actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
   418	`motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`

   421

   423	
   424	This one shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.
   425	
   426	**`width` / `height` / `boxSize` / `min|maxWidth` / `min|maxHeight` resolve through `theme.sizes`.
   427	`margin` / `padding` / `gap` / `top`-`right`-`bottom`-`left` resolve through `theme.space`.**
   428	
   429	The Zimmermann named scale (`xs`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`…) is registered as **`space` only** — deliberately,
   430	for the collision reason above. So a scale key on a *sizing* prop falls through to **Chakra's default
   431	`sizes`**, which reuses the same names for completely different values:

   446	properties only.
   447

   449	exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and
   450	the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.
   451	
   452	#### Four more layout traps, all found by rendering rather than by any tool
   453	
   454	**A shorthand resets a longhand you declared above it — in your own recipe.** The note above about not
   455	introducing a shorthand where the *base* sets longhands has a sibling: order matters inside your own
   456	object too.
   457	
   458	```ts
   459	paddingBlock: '4.5px',
   460	// …twelve lines later…
   461	padding: 0,          // ← silently wipes paddingBlock
   462	```
   463

# FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery

**Owner:** Marcel Angelo Navarro · **Started:** August 2026

This is the guide to building the UI manually — not via a Figma-to-React generator. F2R outputs are an
input we leverage where they exist; they are not the delivery mechanism. You are writing the component.

Read §3 (Design Foundations) before your first component. It contains traps that will cost you time
each if you meet them by surprise.

---

## 1. The Operating Principles

Four things were agreed that change how you build. They apply to every story.

### Static-first

Where an integration isn't available yet, **build against static data and move on.** Do not block, and
do not stub out a fake integration layer.

- Props in, markup out. The component takes the data it renders as props.
- Static/mock data lives in the **story**, not in the component.
- No data-fetching hooks inside `overrides/app/components/` — that's the container/presentational rule
  in `.claude/rules/components.md`, and it's what makes the later wiring a one-file change instead of
  a rewrite.

When Contentful (or SFCC, or Omneo) comes online, the component doesn't change — the page or container
that feeds it does. If you find yourself writing "temporary" fetch logic inside a component, stop:
that's the thing static-first exists to prevent.

### Leverage what exists before building

In priority order — this is the ladder, and you should be able to say which rung you landed on:

```
Salesforce / PWA Kit base capability
        ↓  nothing fits
Existing shared component in overrides/
        ↓  nothing fits
Existing pattern in the codebase
        ↓  nothing fits
New implementation  ← justify this in the PR description
```

F2R outputs count as "existing": the onshore design team's outputs, Jersey's work (currently mostly
primitive/foundation-level), and the design foundations now in the codebase. Use them where they fit
rather than starting clean.

**The default is override, not build.** Not for tidiness — because an override **inherits the wiring for
free.** Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart
modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of
those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed — none of which is visible in the story points, and
all of which lands on you.

There's a second effect worth understanding, because it changes where your work shows up. PWA Kit's
resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
already import means the entire base template inherits your version** — zero call sites touched. A
bespoke component in a new folder only reaches the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same result
on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site.

⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel
(`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from
'./Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import
that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>/` intercepts
nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not
an interception point. See "Two component families" below.

If you do land on "build custom", expect to justify it in the PR — that's not a formality, it's the one
question review will always ask.

### Figma stays open the whole time

Figma is not a one-time handoff you read and close. Keep it open and use it to actively find problems:

- Validate the build against the design as you go, not at the end.
- Spot **missing tokens** — a value in Figma with no counterpart in `theme/foundation/`.
- Spot **missing design definitions** — a state (hover, disabled, error, empty) with no design.
- Catch discrepancies between design and implementation.

When you find a gap, **raise it** — §7 covers where it goes. Silently inventing a value is the failure
mode; a hardcoded hex that "looked right" is how a design system dies.

**Check the Figma link on the card actually points at your story's frame.** Because we work through the
Figma MCP, that link isn't a reference — it's effectively the spec, and whatever it points at is what
gets built.

A wrong or stale link doesn't announce itself. It produces a component built to the wrong design, AC
signed off against a different frame, and QA testing a third source — none of which surfaces until page
assembly. If the link looks wrong, **ask the BA (Jas) to fix the card**, don't just work it out in a DM.
A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — which the BA and QA both read —
still wrong.

### Ask in the group chat

Work it out together rather than solo. If you've been stuck more than ~30 minutes, or you're about to
make a decision that affects more than your own component, post it. These threads are how the team
learns as a group — a question you think is basic is usually three people's question.

Claude is part of the workflow where it fits. Treat its output the way you'd treat a colleague's
first draft: useful, and checked before it ships.

### The bar you're building to

Worth knowing, because it explains why review here is stricter than you may be used to:
**the SOW allows no more than 10 defects across the build, and no Sev3.**

Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination removes the usual
"ship it, fix it in QA" option — a visual defect that would be a shrug elsewhere consumes part of a very
small budget. Practically, for you:

- Expect UI PRs to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma, not just the diff.
- Self-review the same way before you open it (§8). It's faster than a review round-trip.
- Where design is missing or contradictory, **flag it** rather than picking something plausible. An
  invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence — two problems instead of none.

---

## 2. Before you write any code

Five minutes here saves a day later.

### Run the session start

```bash
/session-start
```

Reads the tracking docs, checks your branch, states where the project is. Do it once per session.

### Confirm your branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

`feature/*` or `fix/*`, branched from `develop`. **If it says `develop` or `main`, stop.** No exceptions.

### Check what already exists

| Question | Where to look |
|---|---|
| Does a Base / Override / Custom component already cover this? | `.claude/registry/components.md` |
| Same for hooks, utils, pages, routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` |
| Which tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier <path>` |
| Is another squad the owner? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squad{A,B}.md` |

The registry's **`Origin`** column is the one that matters most:

- **`Custom`** — a Zimmermann component already in `overrides/`. Extend it.
- **`Override`** — a base component already scaffolded into `overrides/`. Edit it directly.
- **`Base`** — it exists upstream but is **not** in `overrides/` yet. **This has a cost.** See below.

### Three component families — and they do different jobs

`overrides/app/components/` holds three kinds of thing. Knowing which you're writing decides the path, the
naming, and whether it affects anything but your own page.

| | `components/<kebab-name>/` | `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules}/<camelName>/` | `components/shared/ui/<PascalName>/` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | An override of an SFCC component | A Zimmermann design-system component | A raw primitive — Link, Text, Image, Button |
| **Naming** | Keep SFCC's kebab-case exactly (`product-tile/`) | **camelCase** (`zimmButton/`) | Mirror upstream's PascalCase (`Button/`) |
| **Layout** | `index.tsx` + story | `index.tsx` + story, one folder per component | `index.tsx` |
| **Intercepts SFCC?** | **Yes** — base files import by full package path | No | **No** — see the barrel exception above |
| **Who consumes it** | Every base page that used it, plus you | Our own pages and components | Explicit importers — chiefly Contentful renderers |
| **Reach for it when** | Changing how an SFCC component looks or behaves | Building a Zimmermann component from the F2R design library | You want a plain branded primitive, no commerce semantics |

The `shared/ui` family exists because **Contentful renderers need primitives, not commerce components.**
Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection` (`Box`, `Text`),
`collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup` (`Box`, `Image`, `Link`, `Skeleton`,
`Text`), `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `shoppableImage`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra
(`shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`). A CMS rich-text
renderer mapping a `hyperlink` node to a `Link` wants exactly that — predictable and unopinionated — not a
component carrying SFCC's locale-routing and commerce behaviour.

**Status: the intent is agreed, the wiring is not built.** A `shared/ui/Button` exists on
`feature/pdp-token-class-spike`, its only consumer is the `/dev/components` catalogue page, there is no
`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx` barrel, and `collectionHero` still imports `Button` from
the SFCC barrel — so it still gets raw Chakra. Don't build against this family until the barrel question
is settled (see the playbook).

### Atoms and molecules — where they go and what they're called

**Decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live under:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/       zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/   zimmInputAction/
  organisms/   (when the first one lands)
               └── index.tsx  +  index.stories.tsx
```

**Naming is `camelCase`, one folder per component, `index.tsx` inside.** That follows
`conventions.md` — these are Zimmermann-authored, so camelCase; the kebab-case rule applies *only* to files
mirroring a base Salesforce file, and there is no `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` to mirror. It also satisfies
`components.md`'s rule that **the named export matches the folder name** — `zimmButton/` exports
`ZimmButton`. Precedents already in the repo: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`.

Three casings exist and each is correct in its own family — don't generalise from one to another:

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Must match upstream; their files import that path |
| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | **Zimmermann-authored — the default rule** |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own PascalCase exactly |

**Which tier?** Atom / molecule / organism is decided by **what the component's own template renders**,
not by how big it looks:

- **Atom** — renders no other component. Markup, CSS and tokens only.
- **Molecule** — renders only atoms.
- **Organism** — renders at least one molecule.

Two rules that settle most arguments: **an icon passed as a prop doesn't count** (`icon="close"` keeps a
Button an atom), and **slotted children don't count** — only what your own template renders. A top bar
composing just Button + Logo is a molecule even though it spans the viewport; tier follows composition,
not pixel size.

If you're porting from the F2R design library, the tier is already recorded there as `composes: [...]` —
use it rather than re-deriving. Add a `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` line in the JSDoc so
the link back to the contract survives.

### What's actually overridden today

Worth knowing before you estimate anything: **`overrides/app/components/` currently contains seven
directories.** As of `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`:

```
_app-config   button   contentful   foundation   header   icons   pageContainer
```

That's it. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`** — they exist upstream and are
referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` and the protected-file lists, but they have **not** been scaffolded
into `overrides/` yet.

Two consequences:

- **Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first** (below). Assume it until the registry says otherwise.
- **When a rules file points at one of those as an example, the file won't be there.** The convention is
  real; the worked example often isn't yet. Check before you go looking.

### If `Origin = Base`, the copy-first rule applies

Before any functional work, AGENTS.md requires:

1. Copy the base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` (keep the kebab-case filename exactly)
2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` marker
5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override is rendering instead of the base
6. Then build; remove the markers

It's serialised and human-gated, and **the first story against a given base component pays it — later
ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement,
not on day three of the sprint.

### Sanity-check the scope

```bash
/scope-check
```

Classifies everything you're about to touch by tier and tells you if the change is safe, risky, or
blocked. Worth it any time you're not certain.

---

Work it out together rather than solo. If you've been stuck more than ~30 minutes, or you're about to
make a decision that affects more than your own component, post it. These threads are how the team
learns as a group — a question you think is basic is usually three people's question.

Claude is part of the workflow where it fits. Treat its output the way you'd treat a colleague's
first draft: useful, and checked before it ships.

### The bar you're building to

Worth knowing, because it explains why review here is stricter than you may be used to:
**the SOW allows no more than 10 defects across the build, and no Sev3.**

Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination removes the usual
"ship it, fix it in QA" option — a visual defect that would be a shrug elsewhere consumes part of a very
small budget. Practically, for you:

- Expect UI PRs to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma, not just the diff.
- Self-review the same way before you open it (§8). It's faster than a review round-trip.
- Where design is missing or contradictory, **flag it** rather than picking something plausible. An
  invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence — two problems instead of none.

---

## 2. Before you write any code

Five minutes here saves a day later.

### Run the session start

```bash
/session-start
```

Reads the tracking docs, checks your branch, states where the project is. Do it once per session.

### Confirm your branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

`feature/*` or `fix/*`, branched from `develop`. **If it says `develop` or `main`, stop.** No exceptions.

### Check what already exists

| Question | Where to look |
|---|---|
| Does a Base / Override / Custom component already cover this? | `.claude/registry/components.md` |
| Same for hooks, utils, pages, routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` |
| Which tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier <path>` |
| Is another squad the owner? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squad{A,B}.md` |

The registry's **`Origin`** column is the one that matters most:

- **`Custom`** — a Zimmermann component already in `overrides/`. Extend it.
- **`Override`** — a base component already scaffolded into `overrides/`. Edit it directly.
- **`Base`** — it exists upstream but is **not** in `overrides/` yet. **This has a cost.** See below.

### Three component families — and they do different jobs

`overrides/app/components/` holds three kinds of thing. Knowing which you're writing decides the path, the
naming, and whether it affects anything but your own page.

| | `components/<kebab-name>/` | `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules}/<camelName>/` | `components/shared/ui/<PascalName>/` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | An override of an SFCC component | A Zimmermann design-system component | A raw primitive — Link, Text, Image, Button |
| **Naming** | Keep SFCC's kebab-case exactly (`product-tile/`) | **camelCase** (`zimmButton/`) | Mirror upstream's PascalCase (`Button/`) |
| **Layout** | `index.tsx` + story | `index.tsx` + story, one folder per component | `index.tsx` |
| **Intercepts SFCC?** | **Yes** — base files import by full package path | No | **No** — see the barrel exception above |
| **Who consumes it** | Every base page that used it, plus you | Our own pages and components | Explicit importers — chiefly Contentful renderers |
| **Reach for it when** | Changing how an SFCC component looks or behaves | Building a Zimmermann component from the F2R design library | You want a plain branded primitive, no commerce semantics |

The `shared/ui` family exists because **Contentful renderers need primitives, not commerce components.**
Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection` (`Box`, `Text`),
`collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup` (`Box`, `Image`, `Link`, `Skeleton`,
`Text`), `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `shoppableImage`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra
(`shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`). A CMS rich-text
renderer mapping a `hyperlink` node to a `Link` wants exactly that — predictable and unopinionated — not a
component carrying SFCC's locale-routing and commerce behaviour.

**Status: the intent is agreed, the wiring is not built.** A `shared/ui/Button` exists on
`feature/pdp-token-class-spike`, its only consumer is the `/dev/components` catalogue page, there is no
`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx` barrel, and `collectionHero` still imports `Button` from
the SFCC barrel — so it still gets raw Chakra. Don't build against this family until the barrel question
is settled (see the playbook).

### Atoms and molecules — where they go and what they're called

**Decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live under:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/       zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/   zimmInputAction/
  organisms/   (when the first one lands)
               └── index.tsx  +  index.stories.tsx
```

**Naming is `camelCase`, one folder per component, `index.tsx` inside.** That follows
`conventions.md` — these are Zimmermann-authored, so camelCase; the kebab-case rule applies *only* to files
mirroring a base Salesforce file, and there is no `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` to mirror. It also satisfies
`components.md`'s rule that **the named export matches the folder name** — `zimmButton/` exports
`ZimmButton`. Precedents already in the repo: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`.

Three casings exist and each is correct in its own family — don't generalise from one to another:

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Must match upstream; their files import that path |
| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | **Zimmermann-authored — the default rule** |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own PascalCase exactly |

**Which tier?** Atom / molecule / organism is decided by **what the component's own template renders**,
not by how big it looks:

- **Atom** — renders no other component. Markup, CSS and tokens only.
- **Molecule** — renders only atoms.
- **Organism** — renders at least one molecule.

Two rules that settle most arguments: **an icon passed as a prop doesn't count** (`icon="close"` keeps a
Button an atom), and **slotted children don't count** — only what your own template renders. A top bar
composing just Button + Logo is a molecule even though it spans the viewport; tier follows composition,
not pixel size.

If you're porting from the F2R design library, the tier is already recorded there as `composes: [...]` —
use it rather than re-deriving. Add a `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` line in the JSDoc so
the link back to the contract survives.

### What's actually overridden today

Worth knowing before you estimate anything: **`overrides/app/components/` currently contains seven
directories.** As of `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`:

```
_app-config   button   contentful   foundation   header   icons   pageContainer
```

That's it. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`** — they exist upstream and are
referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` and the protected-file lists, but they have **not** been scaffolded
into `overrides/` yet.

Two consequences:

- **Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first** (below). Assume it until the registry says otherwise.
- **When a rules file points at one of those as an example, the file won't be there.** The convention is
  real; the worked example often isn't yet. Check before you go looking.

### If `Origin = Base`, the copy-first rule applies

Before any functional work, AGENTS.md requires:

1. Copy the base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` (keep the kebab-case filename exactly)
2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` marker
5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override is rendering instead of the base
6. Then build; remove the markers

It's serialised and human-gated, and **the first story against a given base component pays it — later
ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement,
not on day three of the sprint.

### Sanity-check the scope

```bash
/scope-check
```

Classifies everything you're about to touch by tier and tells you if the change is safe, risky, or
blocked. Worth it any time you're not certain.

## 3. Design Foundations — read this before your first component

**Canonical reference: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`.** That file is the authority on styling an
override; this section is the orientation for it. If the two ever disagree, the rules file wins — and
this section needs a fix, so raise it.

The design system lives in `overrides/app/theme/`. It has **one** source of truth and derives outward:

```
foundation/  colour.ts · typography.ts · spacing.ts · sizes.ts · motion.ts · gridSystem.ts
        |  imported and derived from — never retyped
foundation/zimmTokens.ts          -> the --zimm-* CSS custom properties
        |  consumed by
theme/components/*.ts (recipes)   ·   globalStyles.ts (.zimm-* classes)
```

`zimmTokens.ts` is **derived**, not a second copy — it imports `colors.grey[900]` rather than retyping
`#191919`. That is why you never edit it directly, and why two values cannot drift apart.
`theme/index.test.tsx` guards the arrangement with 125 tests; a failure there is a real drift signal,
not test noise.

### The styling hierarchy — reach for these in order

This is the load-bearing rule of the whole section.

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`
2. **Semantic token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`
3. **The component's own `theme/components/<name>.ts`** for anything that varies by variant / size /
   state. For an interactive component with Chakra support (buttons, inputs, links) that file is the
   **single source of truth**
4. **`sx` prop** for a genuine one-off gap in the Chakra prop system
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` truly cannot express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes)

**Never** a raw hex / px / rem / em literal in a component file. The one standing exception is
`button.ts`'s provisional constants — trap 2 below.

Registered component recipes today: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` (`theme/components/index.ts`).
Adding a new one is yours to do — one file per Chakra component, registered in that index.

### Setting type — always `textStyle`, never `fontSize`

```tsx
<Text textStyle="body1">…</Text>          // ✅
<Heading textStyle="heading3">…</Heading>  // ✅
<Text fontSize="md">…</Text>               // ❌ never
```

**Why this is a hard rule, not a preference.** Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra
defaults, and the base retail-react-app uses those names at ~199 call sites:

| Key | Zimmermann | Chakra |
|---|---|---|
| `md` | 24px | 16px |
| `xs` | 16px | 12px |
| `2xs` | 14px | 10px |
| `3xs` | 12px | 7.2px |

The Zimmermann font scale is **deliberately not registered** as `theme.fontSizes` for exactly this
reason. If you write `fontSize="md"` expecting 24px you get 16px. If you "fix" that by registering the
scale, you silently restyle every base component on the site. There's a test guarding against it —
don't fight it, use `textStyle`.

**The 22 available text styles:**

`heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` ·
`mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` ·
`button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`

Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation → Typography**.

### Colour — use the semantic aliases

```tsx
<Box bg="background.01" color="text.default" borderColor="border.default" />   // ✅
<Box bg="#f9f8f6" color="#191919" />                                          // ❌
```

Two layers exist. Reach for the **semantic** layer; the primitives are what the semantics are built from.

| Group | Keys |
|---|---|
| `text.*` | `default` `inverse` `inverseGrey` `secondary` `muted` |
| `background.*` | `01`–`07` (`01`–`04` light/ivory, `05`–`06` dark, `07` white) |
| `border.*` | `default` `secondary` `focus` `forms` `error` |
| `status.*` | `success` `error` `errorBackground` `storeClosed` |
| `link.*` · `icon.*` | `default` `hover` · `default` |
| `action.primary.*` | `bgDefault` `bgHover` `bgPressed` `bgDisabled` `bgFocused` `text` `textDisabled` |
| `action.secondary.*` | `border` `bgHover` `text` `textInverse` `textDisabled` |
| Primitives | `grey.{black,900,800,700,600,500,300,200,100,white}` `ivory.{100..400}` `coral/green/orange/red.500` `opacity.{15,30,40,50}` |

Browse under **Foundation → Colour**.

### Spacing

Both scales work — Chakra's numerics are preserved and the Zimmermann named scale is added on top.
**Prefer the named scale**, since it's what the design system speaks:

```tsx
<Box padding="m" marginBottom="xl" />   // ✅ 1rem, 1.5rem
<Box padding={4} />                      // works, but not the design vocabulary
```

`3xs` 0.125 · `2xs` 0.25 · `xs` 0.5 · `s` 0.75 · `m` 1 · `l` 1.25 · `xl` 1.5 · `2xl` 2 · `3xl` 2.5 ·
`4xl` 4 · `5xl` 5 · `6xl` 8 · `7xl` 10 — **in `rem`**, i.e. 2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/64/80/128/160px at
the default 16px root font-size.

**The scale is `rem`, not `px`** — spacing and type scale with the user's root font-size and browser
zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). Hairline geometry deliberately does not:

- `borderWidth="default"` → `1px`, registered as a Chakra scale
- `focusRingOffsets.{default, secondary}` → `2px` / `3px`, imported as a constant from
  `app/theme/foundation` (`secondary` exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border)

**Unit rule:** `rem` for anything that should scale (type, spacing) · `px` only for hairline geometry
(border widths, focus-ring offsets) · `em` only for breakpoints. Never a raw literal of any unit in a
component file.

⚠️ **Don't use the `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** You'll see them in `zimmTokens.ts`
(`--zimm-scale-500`, `--zimm-scale-1100`, …). They exist **only** so the `.zimm-*` global classes have
something to reference. The named scale is the Chakra-facing surface:

```tsx
<Box mb="var(--zimm-scale-500)" />   // ❌ 20px, but bypasses the scale
<Box mb="l" />                        // ✅ same 20px, traceable to the token
```

If the value you need has no named entry — 28px and 44px are both in use with nothing between `xl` (24)
and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64) — that's a **token gap to raise** (§7), not a reason to reach
for the numeric alias.

### Icon sizes, action sizes and motion are NOT theme tokens

These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere),
so they're **imported as constants** instead:

```tsx
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';

<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                                    // 20px
<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />                          // 52px
transition: `opacity ${motion.duration.fast} ${motion.easing.standard}`
```

`iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
`actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
`motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`

⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL** and pending designer sign-off. Use them, but expect them to move.

#### The trap: a spacing token key on a sizing prop

This one shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.

**`width` / `height` / `boxSize` / `min|maxWidth` / `min|maxHeight` resolve through `theme.sizes`.
`margin` / `padding` / `gap` / `top`-`right`-`bottom`-`left` resolve through `theme.space`.**

The Zimmermann named scale (`xs`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`…) is registered as **`space` only** — deliberately,
for the collision reason above. So a scale key on a *sizing* prop falls through to **Chakra's default
`sizes`**, which reuses the same names for completely different values:

```tsx
// theme/components/footer.ts — intended a 24px icon touch target
width: 'xl',    // ❌ → var(--chakra-sizes-xl) = 36rem = 576px
height: 'xl',   // ❌   every contact icon became 576px; the footer layout collapsed on every page

width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',   // ✅ 1.5rem = 24px — literal CSS, no scale lookup
```

Chakra's `sizes` are container widths: `xs` 20rem · `sm` 24rem · `md` 28rem · `lg` 32rem · `xl` 36rem.
Each is a plausible-looking, silent 20–30× blow-up.

**The rule:** on a sizing property use `var(--zimm-scale-*)`, an imported constant (`iconSizes`,
`actionSizes`), or an explicit unit — **never a bare scale key**. Bare keys are safe on spacing
properties only.

Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied, no lint rule
exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and
the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.

#### Four more layout traps, all found by rendering rather than by any tool

**A shorthand resets a longhand you declared above it — in your own recipe.** The note above about not
introducing a shorthand where the *base* sets longhands has a sibling: order matters inside your own
object too.

```ts
paddingBlock: '4.5px',
// …twelve lines later…
padding: 0,          // ← silently wipes paddingBlock
```

The first attempt at the footer nav item had exactly this and appeared to do nothing at all. Use
`paddingInline: 0` when you mean "no horizontal padding". `recipeGuards.test.ts` catches a bare scale key
*inside* a shorthand; it does not catch this.

**A wrapped element takes the width available to it, not the width of its longest line.** The footer's
ABOUT column sat at its 160px cap while its longest rendered line was 115px — 45px of dead space that
pushed the next column right. `width: min-content` resolves to the widest *unbreakable run*, which is
what you want — but only for a label whose break is deliberate. On a single-line label it collapses to
the longest word and wraps it. Gate it on a signal that means "this break is intentional".

**Height from `minHeight` + `align-items: center` breaks the moment content wraps.** Centring only
distributes what a single line leaves over. A two-line label overflows the floor, so the leading
collapses to zero and the item sits flush against the one above. Derive height from `lineHeight` plus
padding instead — it holds at any line count.

**A block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` leaks ~1.5px per row.** The line box's strut adds
descender space below the baseline. Five rows cost 9px against Figma. `display: flex` on the list item
removes the line box entirely; axe confirmed list semantics survive.

#### Figma's text boxes are cap-height. Browser line boxes are not.

Figma reports a single-line footer item as 8px of text and two lines as 22px; the same text in a browser
measures ~14.5px and ~29px. **Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** For the nav item the rule was "equal
space above and below, height follows the line count" — expressed in our units as `lineHeight: 14px` plus
4.5px block padding, which lands on Figma's 24px and 38px exactly. Copying 8/22 would have produced
nonsense.

#### Type metrics change layout decisions — get the real font in first

Before the real faces were served, the fallback stack rendered roughly **13% wider**. Several sizing
decisions taken against it were simply wrong and had to be redone: a nav-column cap chosen to make one
label wrap stopped working once labels shrank, and a 768px overflow disappeared on its own. If a build
depends on measured text, self-host the font before you start measuring.

#### When no single value satisfies two constraints, constrain the text instead

The ACK label needed to wrap after the first word while "BOOK AN APPOINTMENT" stayed on one line. The
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px**, a coincidence rather than a tolerance. A non-breaking
space between the words that must stay together widened the safe window to 71px. Content-level fixes are
sometimes the robust ones — but note the dependency: production copy has to carry the same character.

### The `.zimm-*` global classes — and the one rule about them

**27** global classes exist: `.zimm-text-*` (typography), `.zimm-form-*` (form-field layout),
`.zimm-grid`, `.zimm-focus-visible`. They mirror the design system as static CSS so handover markup can
be pasted and look right. They are **not** the preferred authoring route for new Zimmermann components —
default to the hierarchy above.

**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** The whole family was deleted
deliberately, and the reason generalises:

> **One canonical styling surface per component type.** If a component has interactive state, its
> `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe is the only place its look is defined. A static CSS class cannot
> express `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" of a recipe is
> structurally incomplete from birth — and nothing stops the two drifting apart afterwards.

So: **every button is Chakra's `<Button>` styled by `theme/components/button.ts`.** Never a class, never
a hand-rolled `<button>` with its own styles. `.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool only for genuinely
static, non-interactive, heavily-reused treatments — typography, the grid, form-field layout.

⚠️ Worth knowing: `globalStyles.ts` has almost no consumers today (one Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`)
and it ships on every page. Don't reach for a class where a prop or a recipe will do.

### Interaction state goes in CSS, never in React state

This is the rule most likely to cost you a rewrite, so it's worth being blunt about.

Hover, press, focus and disabled belong in the component's theme recipe as Chakra's pseudo-props. They do
**not** belong in `useState`.

```tsx
// ❌ never — interaction state in React
const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false)
<button onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(true)} style={{background: hovered ? a : b}}>

// ✅ theme/components/myThing.ts — the browser does the work
_hover:        { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover)' },
_active:       { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-pressed)' },
_disabled:     { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-border-secondary)', cursor: 'not-allowed' },
_focusVisible: { outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)' },
```

It looks identical in a screenshot. It behaves differently in five ways that all matter here:

| JS state | CSS pseudo-class |
|---|---|
| Dead until hydration — the button renders but doesn't respond | Works on first paint, no JS needed |
| No way to express `@media (hover: hover)` → sticky hover on touch after a tap | Opts out on touch devices properly |
| Inline styles win every specificity fight — the theme **cannot** override them | Overridable by variant, later |
| The keyboard focus ring built for WCAG 2.4.7 lives in the recipe, so it never applies | Inherited automatically |
| Every hover re-renders the component | No React work at all |

With a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget and a WCAG 2.2 AA target, the first and fourth rows are the ones that
turn into defects.

**Corollary — a theme recipe nothing consumes is dead code.** If you write
`theme/components/myThing.ts` and register it, the component has to actually read it — Chakra's
`<Button>`/`<Link>` etc. do so automatically; a custom multipart component needs
`useStyleConfig('MyThing')`. A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.

### The styling surface for a ui-kit component — decided

**A theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a co-located CSS file. Pick the
case that matches what you're building:

| Case | What you write |
|---|---|
| It **is** a Chakra component (`Button`, `Link`, `Input`) | A recipe at `theme/components/<name>.ts`. Chakra resolves `variant`/`size` automatically — your component is a thin prop-mapping layer |
| A **bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | A recipe + register it + read it with `useMultiStyleConfig` + build on the `chakra()` factory |
| Genuinely **static, non-interactive, heavily reused** | A `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` |
| Nothing above fits | `sx`, then a co-located `.scss` — last resort, per `css.md` |

**The bespoke case, worked** — this is the one people get stuck on, because a recipe can't style a bare
`<input>`. The `chakra()` factory is the bridge: it makes a native element theme-aware, so you keep native
semantics *and* get recipe styling.

```ts
// theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts
import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
// Figma node 40000265:374 — field/border/* tokens
const BORDER = { default: 'var(--zimm-color-border-forms)', … } as const;
export const ZimmTextInput = { parts: [...], baseStyle: {...}, variants: {...} };
```
```ts
// theme/components/index.ts — register it, or destructuring throws at runtime
export const components = { Button, Footer, Header, ListMenu, ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput };
```
```tsx
// components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', { inverse, disabled });
```

Note the theme key is **PascalCase** (`ZimmTextInput`) while the file is camelCase
(`zimmTextInput.ts`) — the key is the Chakra component name, the filename follows our convention. Same
split as `listMenu.ts` → `ListMenu`.
