theme/components/*.ts (recipes)   ·   globalStyles.ts (.zimm-* classes)
```

`zimmTokens.ts` is **derived**, not a second copy — it imports `colors.grey[900]` rather than retyping
`#191919`. That is why you never edit it directly, and why two values cannot drift apart.
`theme/index.test.tsx` guards the arrangement with 125 tests; a failure there is a real drift signal,
not test noise.

### The styling hierarchy — reach for these in order

This is the load-bearing rule of the whole section.

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`
2. **Semantic token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`
3. **The component's own `theme/components/<name>.ts`** for anything that varies by variant / size /
   state. For an interactive component with Chakra support (buttons, inputs, links) that file is the
   **single source of truth**
4. **`sx` prop** for a genuine one-off gap in the Chakra prop system
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` truly cannot express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes)

**Never** a raw hex / px / rem / em literal in a component file. The one standing exception is
`button.ts`'s provisional constants — trap 2 below.

Registered component recipes today: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` (`theme/components/index.ts`).
Adding a new one is yours to do — one file per Chakra component, registered in that index.

### Setting type — always `textStyle`, never `fontSize`

```tsx
<Text textStyle="body1">…</Text>          // ✅
<Heading textStyle="heading3">…</Heading>  // ✅
<Text fontSize="md">…</Text>               // ❌ never
```

**Why this is a hard rule, not a preference.** Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra
defaults, and the base retail-react-app uses those names at ~199 call sites:

| Key | Zimmermann | Chakra |
|---|---|---|
| `md` | 24px | 16px |
| `xs` | 16px | 12px |
| `2xs` | 14px | 10px |
| `3xs` | 12px | 7.2px |

The Zimmermann font scale is **deliberately not registered** as `theme.fontSizes` for exactly this
reason. If you write `fontSize="md"` expecting 24px you get 16px. If you "fix" that by registering the
scale, you silently restyle every base component on the site. There's a test guarding against it —
don't fight it, use `textStyle`.

**The 22 available text styles:**

`heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` ·
`mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` ·
`button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`

Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation → Typography**.

### Colour — use the semantic aliases

```tsx
<Box bg="background.01" color="text.default" borderColor="border.default" />   // ✅
<Box bg="#f9f8f6" color="#191919" />                                          // ❌
```

Two layers exist. Reach for the **semantic** layer; the primitives are what the semantics are built from.

| Group | Keys |
|---|---|
| `text.*` | `default` `inverse` `inverseGrey` `secondary` `muted` |
| `background.*` | `01`–`07` (`01`–`04` light/ivory, `05`–`06` dark, `07` white) |
| `border.*` | `default` `secondary` `focus` `forms` `error` |
| `status.*` | `success` `error` `errorBackground` `storeClosed` |
| `link.*` · `icon.*` | `default` `hover` · `default` |
| `action.primary.*` | `bgDefault` `bgHover` `bgPressed` `bgDisabled` `bgFocused` `text` `textDisabled` |
| `action.secondary.*` | `border` `bgHover` `text` `textInverse` `textDisabled` |
| Primitives | `grey.{black,900,800,700,600,500,300,200,100,white}` `ivory.{100..400}` `coral/green/orange/red.500` `opacity.{15,30,40,50}` |

Browse under **Foundation → Colour**.

### Spacing

Both scales work — Chakra's numerics are preserved and the Zimmermann named scale is added on top.
**Prefer the named scale**, since it's what the design system speaks:

```tsx
<Box padding="m" marginBottom="xl" />   // ✅ 1rem, 1.5rem
<Box padding={4} />                      // works, but not the design vocabulary
```

`3xs` 0.125 · `2xs` 0.25 · `xs` 0.5 · `s` 0.75 · `m` 1 · `l` 1.25 · `xl` 1.5 · `2xl` 2 · `3xl` 2.5 ·
`4xl` 4 · `5xl` 5 · `6xl` 8 · `7xl` 10 — **in `rem`**, i.e. 2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/64/80/128/160px at
the default 16px root font-size.

**The scale is `rem`, not `px`** — spacing and type scale with the user's root font-size and browser
zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). Hairline geometry deliberately does not:

- `borderWidth="default"` → `1px`, registered as a Chakra scale
- `focusRingOffsets.{default, secondary}` → `2px` / `3px`, imported as a constant from
  `app/theme/foundation` (`secondary` exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border)

**Unit rule:** `rem` for anything that should scale (type, spacing) · `px` only for hairline geometry
(border widths, focus-ring offsets) · `em` only for breakpoints. Never a raw literal of any unit in a
component file.

⚠️ **Don't use the `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** You'll see them in `zimmTokens.ts`
(`--zimm-scale-500`, `--zimm-scale-1100`, …). They exist **only** so the `.zimm-*` global classes have
something to reference. The named scale is the Chakra-facing surface:

```tsx
<Box mb="var(--zimm-scale-500)" />   // ❌ 20px, but bypasses the scale
<Box mb="l" />                        // ✅ same 20px, traceable to the token
```

If the value you need has no named entry — 28px and 44px are both in use with nothing between `xl` (24)
and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64) — that's a **token gap to raise** (§7), not a reason to reach
for the numeric alias.

### Icon sizes, action sizes and motion are NOT theme tokens

These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere),
so they're **imported as constants** instead:

```tsx
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';

<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                                    // 20px
<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />                          // 52px
transition: `opacity ${motion.duration.fast} ${motion.easing.standard}`
```

`iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
`actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
`motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`

⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL** and pending designer sign-off. Use them, but expect them to move.

#### The trap: a spacing token key on a sizing prop

This one shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.

**`width` / `height` / `boxSize` / `min|maxWidth` / `min|maxHeight` resolve through `theme.sizes`.
`margin` / `padding` / `gap` / `top`-`right`-`bottom`-`left` resolve through `theme.space`.**

The Zimmermann named scale (`xs`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`…) is registered as **`space` only** — deliberately,
for the collision reason above. So a scale key on a *sizing* prop falls through to **Chakra's default
`sizes`**, which reuses the same names for completely different values:

```tsx
// theme/components/footer.ts — intended a 24px icon touch target
width: 'xl',    // ❌ → var(--chakra-sizes-xl) = 36rem = 576px
height: 'xl',   // ❌   every contact icon became 576px; the footer layout collapsed on every page

width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',   // ✅ 1.5rem = 24px — literal CSS, no scale lookup
```

Chakra's `sizes` are container widths: `xs` 20rem · `sm` 24rem · `md` 28rem · `lg` 32rem · `xl` 36rem.
Each is a plausible-looking, silent 20–30× blow-up.

**The rule:** on a sizing property use `var(--zimm-scale-*)`, an imported constant (`iconSizes`,
`actionSizes`), or an explicit unit — **never a bare scale key**. Bare keys are safe on spacing
properties only.

Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied, no lint rule
exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and
the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.

#### Four more layout traps, all found by rendering rather than by any tool

**A shorthand resets a longhand you declared above it — in your own recipe.** The note above about not
introducing a shorthand where the *base* sets longhands has a sibling: order matters inside your own
object too.

```ts
paddingBlock: '4.5px',
// …twelve lines later…
padding: 0,          // ← silently wipes paddingBlock
```

The first attempt at the footer nav item had exactly this and appeared to do nothing at all. Use
`paddingInline: 0` when you mean "no horizontal padding". `recipeGuards.test.ts` catches a bare scale key
*inside* a shorthand; it does not catch this.

**A wrapped element takes the width available to it, not the width of its longest line.** The footer's
ABOUT column sat at its 160px cap while its longest rendered line was 115px — 45px of dead space that
pushed the next column right. `width: min-content` resolves to the widest *unbreakable run*, which is
what you want — but only for a label whose break is deliberate. On a single-line label it collapses to
the longest word and wraps it. Gate it on a signal that means "this break is intentional".

**Height from `minHeight` + `align-items: center` breaks the moment content wraps.** Centring only
distributes what a single line leaves over. A two-line label overflows the floor, so the leading
collapses to zero and the item sits flush against the one above. Derive height from `lineHeight` plus
padding instead — it holds at any line count.

**A block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` leaks ~1.5px per row.** The line box's strut adds
descender space below the baseline. Five rows cost 9px against Figma. `display: flex` on the list item
removes the line box entirely; axe confirmed list semantics survive.

#### Figma's text boxes are cap-height. Browser line boxes are not.

Figma reports a single-line footer item as 8px of text and two lines as 22px; the same text in a browser
measures ~14.5px and ~29px. **Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** For the nav item the rule was "equal
space above and below, height follows the line count" — expressed in our units as `lineHeight: 14px` plus
4.5px block padding, which lands on Figma's 24px and 38px exactly. Copying 8/22 would have produced
nonsense.

#### Type metrics change layout decisions — get the real font in first

Before the real faces were served, the fallback stack rendered roughly **13% wider**. Several sizing
decisions taken against it were simply wrong and had to be redone: a nav-column cap chosen to make one
label wrap stopped working once labels shrank, and a 768px overflow disappeared on its own. If a build
depends on measured text, self-host the font before you start measuring.

#### When no single value satisfies two constraints, constrain the text instead

The ACK label needed to wrap after the first word while "BOOK AN APPOINTMENT" stayed on one line. The
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px**, a coincidence rather than a tolerance. A non-breaking
space between the words that must stay together widened the safe window to 71px. Content-level fixes are
sometimes the robust ones — but note the dependency: production copy has to carry the same character.

### The `.zimm-*` global classes — and the one rule about them

**27** global classes exist: `.zimm-text-*` (typography), `.zimm-form-*` (form-field layout),
`.zimm-grid`, `.zimm-focus-visible`. They mirror the design system as static CSS so handover markup can
be pasted and look right. They are **not** the preferred authoring route for new Zimmermann components —
default to the hierarchy above.

**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** The whole family was deleted
deliberately, and the reason generalises:

> **One canonical styling surface per component type.** If a component has interactive state, its
> `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe is the only place its look is defined. A static CSS class cannot
> express `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" of a recipe is
> structurally incomplete from birth — and nothing stops the two drifting apart afterwards.

So: **every button is Chakra's `<Button>` styled by `theme/components/button.ts`.** Never a class, never
a hand-rolled `<button>` with its own styles. `.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool only for genuinely
static, non-interactive, heavily-reused treatments — typography, the grid, form-field layout.

⚠️ Worth knowing: `globalStyles.ts` has almost no consumers today (one Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`)
and it ships on every page. Don't reach for a class where a prop or a recipe will do.

### Interaction state goes in CSS, never in React state

This is the rule most likely to cost you a rewrite, so it's worth being blunt about.

Hover, press, focus and disabled belong in the component's theme recipe as Chakra's pseudo-props. They do
**not** belong in `useState`.

```tsx
// ❌ never — interaction state in React
const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false)
<button onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(true)} style={{background: hovered ? a : b}}>

// ✅ theme/components/myThing.ts — the browser does the work
_hover:        { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover)' },
_active:       { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-pressed)' },
_disabled:     { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-border-secondary)', cursor: 'not-allowed' },
_focusVisible: { outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)' },
```

It looks identical in a screenshot. It behaves differently in five ways that all matter here:

| JS state | CSS pseudo-class |
|---|---|
| Dead until hydration — the button renders but doesn't respond | Works on first paint, no JS needed |
| No way to express `@media (hover: hover)` → sticky hover on touch after a tap | Opts out on touch devices properly |
| Inline styles win every specificity fight — the theme **cannot** override them | Overridable by variant, later |
| The keyboard focus ring built for WCAG 2.4.7 lives in the recipe, so it never applies | Inherited automatically |
| Every hover re-renders the component | No React work at all |

With a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget and a WCAG 2.2 AA target, the first and fourth rows are the ones that
turn into defects.

**Corollary — a theme recipe nothing consumes is dead code.** If you write
`theme/components/myThing.ts` and register it, the component has to actually read it — Chakra's
`<Button>`/`<Link>` etc. do so automatically; a custom multipart component needs
`useStyleConfig('MyThing')`. A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.

### The styling surface for a ui-kit component — decided

**A theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a co-located CSS file. Pick the
case that matches what you're building:

| Case | What you write |
|---|---|
| It **is** a Chakra component (`Button`, `Link`, `Input`) | A recipe at `theme/components/<name>.ts`. Chakra resolves `variant`/`size` automatically — your component is a thin prop-mapping layer |
| A **bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | A recipe + register it + read it with `useMultiStyleConfig` + build on the `chakra()` factory |
| Genuinely **static, non-interactive, heavily reused** | A `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` |
| Nothing above fits | `sx`, then a co-located `.scss` — last resort, per `css.md` |

**The bespoke case, worked** — this is the one people get stuck on, because a recipe can't style a bare
`<input>`. The `chakra()` factory is the bridge: it makes a native element theme-aware, so you keep native
semantics *and* get recipe styling.

```ts
// theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts
import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
// Figma node 40000265:374 — field/border/* tokens
const BORDER = { default: 'var(--zimm-color-border-forms)', … } as const;
export const ZimmTextInput = { parts: [...], baseStyle: {...}, variants: {...} };
```
```ts
// theme/components/index.ts — register it, or destructuring throws at runtime
export const components = { Button, Footer, Header, ListMenu, ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput };
```
```tsx
// components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', { inverse, disabled });
```

Note the theme key is **PascalCase** (`ZimmTextInput`) while the file is camelCase
(`zimmTextInput.ts`) — the key is the Chakra component name, the filename follows our convention. Same
split as `listMenu.ts` → `ListMenu`.

content.content: **Why not co-located CSS, when plain CSS handles `:hover` perfectly well?** Because a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, and those are **derived output** — the bottom of the token pipeline. Author there and you give up `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the 125 drift-guard tests in `theme/index.test.tsx`. It isn't bad CSS; it's the wrong end of the pipeline. *(You may see `.styles.ts` files using `.zimm-*` classes on the F2R conversion branch. They're a faithful Figma→CSS transcription and excellent raw material for writing a recipe — convert them, don't copy the pattern. `.zimm-btn-*` classes in particular were deliberately removed from `globalStyles.ts`; don't reintroduce them anywhere.)* ### Adding a new token **You don't.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned (Hard Rule #3). If Figma has a value with no token, that's a §7 escalation, not a local addition. Same for `theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, needs a named owner's nod). Per-component theme overrides in `theme/components/` **are** yours to add — one file per Chakra component, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. ### Naming a recipe — `extendTheme` MERGES, it does not replace `theme/index.ts` composes with `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, and that is a **deep merge**. If your recipe key matches an SFCC base recipe key, you are not replacing theirs — **you are inheriting it.** Base SFCC ships recipes for `Footer`, `Header`, `ListMenu`, `Button`, `CheckoutFooter` and more. Register a recipe called `Footer` and every part name you happen to share silently inherits the base's properties. Two failure modes, both seen on this project: **1 · Properties you never chose.** SFCC's `Footer.copyright` is `{fontSize: 'sm', marginBottom: 6}`. Our recipe set `textStyle: 'footer'` (10px) — the base's literal `fontSize: 'sm'` won, so copyright rendered at **14px with a stray 24px bottom margin** nobody wrote. **2 · Reordered output — the dangerous one.** A key that already exists in the base keeps the *base's* position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. So: ```ts // ours subscribeHeading: { margin: 0, /* … */ marginBottom: 'xl' } // 24px gap intended ``` ```css /* merged output — base already had marginBottom, so ours took its early slot; `margin` was new, so it landed last and reset the shorthand */ margin-bottom: var(--chakra-space-xl); /* 24px */ margin: 0px; /* ← wins. Gap is now 0. */ ``` In isolation Chakra emits these in the correct order. **Only the merge inverts them.** **The rule:** - **Full rewrite** (your recipe shares almost nothing with the base) → **namespace the key**: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`, consumed as `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmFooter')`. Same convention `ZimmNavItem` and `ZimmTextInput` already follow. - **Genuine partial override** (you want the base's other parts — `Header`, `ListMenu`, `Button`) → keep the base key, but **never introduce a CSS shorthand on a part where the base sets longhands.** Your `margin`/`padding`/`background`/`border` is appended last and will wipe them. - Always declare your own `parts` array. A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's list, so any Zimmermann part you add is undeclared. To see exactly what you're inheriting, diff the merged recipe against your source: ```js theme.components.Header.baseStyle // merged — what actually applies ``` --- ## 4. The build sequence Four steps, in order. This is the agreed approach. ### Step 1 — Does it already exist? §2. Check the registry and the base package. Report what you found in the PR description, even when the answer is "nothing" — that's the evidence the ladder was walked. ### Step 2 — Use as-is, override/extend, or build custom? | Verdict | When | What you do | |---|---|---| | **Use as-is** | Base behaviour and markup are right; only styling differs | Style it via `theme/components/.ts`. No component file at all | | **Override / extend** | Base structure is right, behaviour or markup needs changing | Copy-first (§2), then modify. **Minimal changes** — don't remove base functionality you weren't asked to touch | | **Build custom** | Nothing upstream is close | `/new-component` scaffolds it. Justify the call in the PR | Most work should land in the first two columns. If you're reaching for "custom" often, raise it — either the ladder isn't being walked or there's a real gap worth naming. **If SFCC's own components import the thing you're overriding, use the bridge pattern.** Check first: ```bash grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/'" \ node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/ ``` Any hits mean base components depend on it, so its **default export must stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour. Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default. Get this wrong and you restyle or break base cart / checkout / account screens you never opened. Where the brand difference is purely token-driven you don't need the split at all — put it in `theme/components/.ts` instead, and leave the default export untouched. ⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in the repo yet.** `overrideStyling.md` describes this pattern using `product-tile` (`CardBaseline` + faithful default), `link`, `image-gallery`, `display-price` and `swatch-group` — **none of which are overrides on `develop` today.** The pattern is the agreed approach; you may well be the one who establishes the first example of it. If you are, say so in the PR so the rule file can be updated to point at something real. ### Step 3 — Execute the swap / override / build Component folder layout (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`): ``` overrides/app/components/productTile/ index.tsx ← the component (named export matching the folder) index.stories.tsx ← mandatory index.test.ts ← only if logic-heavy types.ts ← only if props are shared with siblings productTile.scss ← only if Chakra props genuinely can't express it ``` - **Zimmermann-authored files:** `camelCase` (`productTile.tsx`) - **Override files mirroring a base file:** keep the original kebab-case exactly (`product-tile.tsx`) - **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** No `.js`/`.jsx`, including stories and config - Named export matches the folder; props type is `Props` - Callbacks are `onEventName`; required props non-optional, optional props use `?` - Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored code (`colour`, `centre`) — override files keep upstream spelling verbatim - No magic numbers or strings — name the constant - JSDoc required on anything with ≥2 callers and on every exported hook **Split it up when:** the component passes ~150 lines, branches heavily, or accumulates ≥2 related `useState` calls (→ extract a hook in `overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`). ### Step 4 — Apply the design styles §3. Chakra props first, tokens always, `textStyle` for type. Then check it against Figma at the breakpoints the design defines, and raise what doesn't line up. --- ## 5. Storybook — non-negotiable, and your build surface Every component exported from its folder needs a `*.stories.tsx`. Internal sub-components that only render inside one parent don't — cover their variants through the parent. Build **in** Storybook rather than building and then adding a story. It's the fastest loop you have, and it's the only place a reviewer can see every state at once. ```bash npm run storybook ``` **Two things Storybook will not show you truthfully.** Base-template SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed in `.storybook/main.js`, mirroring the browser build. Any icon sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` therefore renders as an **empty box** in Storybook while rendering correctly in the app. Twelve of `ZimmIcon`'s types are currently in that state. Our own icons in `zimm.tsx` are unaffected — so an icon that appears blank in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal, not a broken glyph. `test-storybook` needs a **built** Storybook (`build-storybook` + a static server), which is what CI does. Pointing it at a running dev server produces wholesale failures that mean nothing. **Categorisation** (drives the sidebar; pick the first that matches): | Category | What goes here | |---|---| | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons | | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — Button, Input, Badge, Link, Checkbox. *Tiebreaker: usable outside a form?* → `Elements/` | | `Layout/` | Global chrome and structure — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination | | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice | | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, NewsletterSignup | | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies | | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven — use mock Contentful data so variants are visible without a live CMS | ```ts export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ commerce-specific → Commerce/ ``` **Content:** every file has a `Default` export. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`, `Empty`) — not for every prop permutation. This is where your static-first data lives. **`play` functions** only where there's interactive behaviour worth asserting — validation on blur, disclosure open/close, focus movement. Query through `within(canvasElement)`, prefer `getByRole` with an accessible name, and import `userEvent` from `@storybook/test` (not `@testing-library/user-event`). ⚠️ **If a component looks wrong in Storybook but right in the app, suspect your imports before your CSS.** `--zimm-*` variables now resolve correctly in Storybook (§3 trap 1). The likely cause is §3 trap 1b: a base-path import of an already-overridden component renders the *base* SFCC version in Storybook and Vitest while working fine in the app. Switch it to a relative import. ### Your branch gets a live URL, automatically Separate from Storybook, and new: every push to a `feature/*` or `fix/*` branch now builds and deploys itself to its own dedicated MRT environment, then posts the URL as a comment on the PR. - Created on first push and **reused** on later pushes — one environment per branch, not per commit. The comment updates in place rather than piling up. - **Torn down automatically** when the PR closes or the branch is deleted. - A real Sydney-hosted (`ap-southeast-2`) storefront with real dev environment variables — not a mock. - Excluded: `fix/release-*` sub-branches and `hotfix/*`. Use it for design review, QA sign-off, and anything cross-device. Nobody needs your branch checked out locally to look at your work, and it's why you should never have to fight over the shared dev target again. ## 9. Hard stops

Non-negotiable. From AGENTS.md.

- **Never work on `develop` or `main`.**
- **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — designer-owned.
- **Never modify** `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` —
  absolute, no approver exception.
- **Never modify test config** — `vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js`.
- **Never add or remove packages** without integration-team approval. Use `npm install`, don't hand-edit
  `package.json`.
- **Never delete files** unless explicitly asked. Propose it and let a human confirm.
- **Never refactor upward** — fixing a component doesn't license changing the hook it calls.
- **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
- **Never reference a later sprint's code** — check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.
- **Never run `npm start`** — ask; the dev server is shared.
- **Never load a third-party script outside a Didomi consent callback.** Fail closed: unknown consent
  state means load nothing.

### Shared-shell coordination

`header/` `footer/` `drawer-menu/` `list-menu/` `seo/` `_app/` `_app-config/` `routes.tsx` are Tier 2
shared shell — **coordinate with the other squad before touching.** Same for
`product-tile/` `product-item/` `display-price/` `image-gallery/` `swatch-group/` (Squad B owns) and
`order-summary/` `promo-code/` `pickup-or-delivery/` (Squad A owns).

---

## 10. Performance — it's a requirement, not a polish pass

Mobile page speed is a top project priority. **LCP budget ≤ 2s at p75 mobile.**

- **Images:** always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-res image at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting:** dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on first render.
- **Data fetching:** request only the fields you need. No waterfalls — parallelise.
- **Third-party scripts:** must not block LCP. `defer`/`async`/post-hydration only, and always behind Didomi.
- **Bundle size:** gated at `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB. Don't introduce a large dependency
  without asking. *(Note: there is currently no CSS budget in CI — that doesn't mean CSS is free.)*

### Paths

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Components | `overrides/app/components/` |
| Hooks | `overrides/app/hooks/` |
| Pages | `overrides/app/pages/` |
| Shared types | `overrides/app/types/{commerce,components,hooks}.ts` |
| Design tokens (Tier 1, read-only) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
| Component theme overrides (yours) | `overrides/app/theme/components/` |
| **Styling rules — canonical, read this** | `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` |
| `--zimm-*` injection (app + Storybook) | `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx` |
| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons/` |
| Registries | `.claude/registry/*.md` |
| Rules | `.claude/rules/*.md` |
| Requirements | `.docs/prd/` · integrations `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` |

**Icons:** import only from `overrides/app/components/icons`. Never from
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is missing, **ask** — don't substitute
a visually different one.

### The eight things people get wrong most

1. **Interaction state in `useState` instead of the recipe's `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible`** →
   identical in a screenshot; dead until hydration, sticky on touch, and unstylable by the theme (§3)
2. `fontSize="md"` instead of `textStyle` → wrong size, silently
3. **A spacing scale key on a sizing prop** — `width: 'xl'` → `theme.sizes.xl` = **36rem**, not
   `space.xl` = 1.5rem. A silent 24× blow-up that no tool catches. Use `var(--zimm-scale-*)` (§3)
4. **Naming a recipe after an SFCC base recipe** — `extendTheme` merges, so `Footer` inherits SFCC's
   `Footer`, and any shorthand you add lands last and wipes the base's longhands. Namespace it
   (`ZimmFooter`) for a rewrite (§3)
5. Importing an already-overridden component by its `@salesforce/...` base path → your story or test
   silently exercises the unstyled **base** component while the app renders fine (§3 trap 1b)
6. A hardcoded hex or px that "matched the design" → no tool catches it; review will. Reaching for a
   `--zimm-scale-NNN` alias instead of the named scale counts as the same mistake
7. Data-fetching inside a `components/` file → makes the later integration a rewrite
8. Skipping copy-first on an `Origin = Base` component → the override never renders and you debug the
   wrong file

**3 and 4 are the two that a screenshot won't reveal and a reviewer won't spot in a diff** — both were
found on SFCC-55 only by rendering the page and measuring it. They are the strongest argument for the
three-surface self-review in §8.

- **Never modify** `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` —

- **Never delete files** unless explicitly asked. Propose it and let a human confirm.
- **Never refactor upward** — fixing a component doesn't license changing the hook it calls.
- **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
- **Never reference a later sprint's code** — check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.

shared shell — **coordinate with the other squad before touching.** Same for

### Commands

```bash

/audit-tier <path>                # tier, owner, blast radius
/scope-check                      # is this prompt safe to run
/new-component                     # scaffold component + story
/code-quality                     # audit before PR
/pr-checklist                     # generate PR description

| What | Where |
|---|---|

| Hooks | `overrides/app/hooks/` |
| Pages | `overrides/app/pages/` |

| Design tokens (Tier 1, read-only) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
| Component theme overrides (yours) | `overrides/app/theme/components/` |

| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons/` |
| Registries | `.claude/registry/*.md` |
| Rules | `.claude/rules/*.md` |

# FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery

**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026

The developer-facing half. This is the sequenced procedure for taking a Zimmermann UI story
from session start to merged PR.

**Companions:** `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why the machine behaves the way it does — read it when
something fails silently) · `fedLead-playbook.md` (the lead role: refinement, estimation,
review culture, escalation).

**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this manual and that file
disagree, **that file wins** — and tell me, because it means this one is stale.

---

## 1. The Operating Principles

### Static-first

Props in, markup out. A component under `overrides/app/components/` receives its data and
renders it. It does not fetch.

Mock data goes in the story — never a temporary fetch you intend to remove. A component that
owns its own data-fetching cannot be reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched,
mocked in Storybook, or composed by a parent that already has it.

**The one exception**, and it is narrow: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks
(`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including a presentational leaf.
They read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, so they don't create the
SSR/Storybook/composition problem the rule exists to prevent. This covers content identical for
every consumer regardless of route — not anything that varies per page.

⚠️ **Their no-Provider behaviour differs and it will bite you in tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades
to fallback text and renders with zero setup. **`useIntl` throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is
mounted by the base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config` — a narrower subtree than you'd expect. Any
Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it.

### Leverage what already exists

Four rungs, in order:

1. **Use the base SFCC component as-is.**
2. **Override it** — mirror the path under `overrides/`, keep the kebab-case filename.
3. **Compose existing ui-kit atoms** into something new.
4. **Build a new component.** Rarest. Justify it.

Before rung 4, check the registry (`.claude/registry/`) and grep `ui-kits/`.

⚠️ **The `shared/ui` barrel is not the leverage play it looks like.** Overriding
`shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branded styling into base cart/checkout/account **does not
work** — `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite,
and 208 base files import the barrel while 0 import the individual module. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §4.

### Figma stays open the whole time

Not at the end. **And check the Jira card's Figma link actually points at your frame** — a
stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,
QA tests a third source. If it's wrong, ask the BA to fix the card rather than working it out
in a DM.

There are **two Figma files** and cross-comparing them produces confident nonsense. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

### Ask in the group chat

Roughly 30 minutes stuck is the trigger. One question at a time.

### The bar you're building to

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3**. That's the whole project, not per sprint. Expect UI PRs
to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma. Self-review the same way before
you open it (§9) — it's faster than a review round-trip.

---

## 2. Before you write any code

### Confirm the branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.

### Check what already exists

Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:

| Origin | Means |
|---|---|
| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |

⚠️ **Do not trust the registry's `Tier` column.** `generateRegistry.mjs:122` hardcodes tier
arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;
tiers are not. For what actually blocks, read `CODEOWNERS`.

### The three component families

| Family | Casing | Example |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Naming a Zimmermann-
authored file in kebab-case falsely signals Salesforce origin — which inverts the convention's
whole purpose.

### Where a new component goes

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
  index.tsx
  index.stories.tsx
  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
```

**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.

### What's actually overridden today

Eleven directories:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**

### The copy-first rule

For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
before any functional change:

1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.

Never bundle this silently with functional work.

---

## 3. Design Foundations

*The longest section, and the part that moves. Read it before your first component.*

### The styling hierarchy

1. **`textStyle`** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. All 22
   Handover text styles are registered.
2. **`var(--zimm-*)`** for colour and spacing.
3. **The component's own recipe** for anything varying by variant/size/state.
4. **`sx`** for a one-off prop-system gap.
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it. In practice: never. There is
   no `.scss` anywhere in the footer or `ui-kits`.

### ⚠️ [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted — bare token strings are now wrong

An earlier revision of this manual taught `color="text.default"` and `padding="m"`, and said
seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was a smell. **That is backwards from the current rule.**

```tsx
// ❌ bare Chakra/theme token string
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

The reason is **house style, not correctness** — a bare key resolves identically, but forces a
reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it's correct.

`textStyle` stays a bare key. It's the one exception: there's no `var()` for the composite.

**In practice this rarely arises**, because brand values mostly shouldn't be in JSX at all.
Measured on `develop`: `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18 recipe files** and exactly **one**
component `.tsx` — a conditional `paddingLeft` no Chakra prop expresses. Type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine gap.

### ⚠️ The trap: a spacing key on a sizing prop

**This shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.**

```tsx
padding: 'xl',   // ✅ reads theme.space.xl
width: 'xl',     // ❌ reads theme.sizes.xl = 36rem = 576px
```

Only `space` is registered. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are not.
Measured blow-up range **8×–112×**. And `s`/`m`/`l` are absent from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are **dropped silently**.

Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied,
no lint rule exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`,
CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.

`recipeGuards.test.ts` now guards it **inside recipes**. It cannot see a JSX prop.

### ⚠️ `extendTheme` MERGES — it does not replace

Name a recipe `Footer` and it deep-merges into base SFCC's `Footer`, inheriting parts you never
wrote. Namespace everything: `ZimmFooter`.

`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate. Anything
else must be namespaced, and `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails the build if it isn't.

⚠️ A recipe unit test **cannot catch this**: `extendTheme` doesn't populate `theme.__cssMap`,
only `ChakraProvider` does. A direct `css()(theme)` assertion passes vacuously.

### Responsive steps are explicit media queries

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  padding: `var(--zimm-scale-4xl) var(--zimm-scale-3xl) ${SPACE_SECTION}`,
},
```

Two reasons. The array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every
step and the guard flags all four. And `BP.desktop` (64em) **conflicts with Chakra's `lg`=62em
/ `xl`=80em**, so a responsive prop silently steps at the wrong width.

### Register the recipe or it throws

Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path.
Co-location is therefore free — but the key must be in `theme/components/index.ts` or
destructuring throws at runtime.

The consumption pattern is always three lines:

```ts
const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';

### Interaction state belongs in CSS, not React state

`_hover`, `_active`, `_focusVisible`, `_disabled` in the recipe. Not `useState` + `onMouseEnter`.
It looks identical in a screenshot and behaves differently in five ways that all matter:
touch devices, keyboard focus, rapid pointer movement, SSR output, and re-render cost.

`:focus-visible` won't appear after a scripted focus move.

### You don't add tokens

A missing token is an escalation to the UI designer (§8), not a number you invent.

If you must ship a placeholder pending sign-off, make it a **named constant with a comment
containing `provisional`, `pending`, or `placeholder`** — `npm run audit:tokens` reads that
comment and downgrades the finding to an acknowledged exception rather than a violation.
`audit-allow: <reason>` works too.

Current state: **19 unacknowledged violations** repo-wide. Don't add to it.

### Compound values and shorthand order

```ts
padding: 'xs 0',        // ❌ emitted verbatim, browser drops it
paddingInline: 0,       // ✅
```

Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value. And a shorthand declared *after* a
longhand resets it — `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` wipes it.

### Figma comparison

Text nodes report a **cap-height box** and are **not comparable** to a CSS line box. Frames and
instances report a **real box** and are. A uniform residual across siblings is measurement; a
varying one is a defect. Full method in `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

## 4. The build sequence

### Step 1 — does it exist?

Registry, then `ui-kits/`, then the base package.

### Step 2 — pick the rung

**Use as-is** → done.

**Override** → copy-first (§2). Keep the kebab-case filename. If the component is used
internally by SFCC's own components, the **default export must stay a faithful port** — full
prop surface, same `forwardRef` — with Zimmermann styling behind a named export. Check with:

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

⚠️ **When importing a component that already has an override, use a relative path**
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path. The resolver is webpack-only — Storybook and Vitest
don't load it, so a base-path import silently renders the **unstyled base component** in both.

**Build custom** → §2's folder layout.

### Step 3 — execute

Named export matching the folder. Props type named for the component, declared at the top of
the file. Move it to `types.ts` only when a sibling file consumes it.

**Split when:** the component function passes ~150 lines, or branching gets deep. **Extract to
a hook when:** there are ≥2 related `useState` that change together, or a `useEffect` has a
non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function.

### Step 4 — apply design styles

Recipe first. `sx` for genuine gaps. Never a raw literal.

| tier | types | entries |
|---|---|---|

### Before you say a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` → it will render. `unknownContentType` → the model was never installed. Use
`limit=1`; the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0`.

### Fetch depth is load-bearing

`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs, a
field access throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire component renders nothing**.
A depth mistake is indistinguishable from a network failure when you're looking at the page.

**Check the Network tab before assuming the component is broken.** Eight distinct failure modes
look identical from the rendered page.

### Gate zero — does it build

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm run test
npm run audit:tokens
npm run build
```

⚠️ **Vitest does not run `play` functions.** Storybook interaction tests are a separate
command against a *built* Storybook.

⚠️ **`lint`, `tsc` and `audit:tokens` are gated nowhere in CI.** If you don't run them, nobody
does. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors.

### Two repo-specific failure modes

content.content:
- **A `develop` merge can delete a declaration your branch depends on.** Re-run `tsc` **after**
  every merge, not just before.
- **The rule can be wrong, not your code.** Several `.claude/rules/` lines currently prescribe
  things that break — `testing.md:87`'s `@storybook/test`, `testing.md:100`'s missing portal
  carve-out. Check the rule against the installed package before contorting the code.

### Three-surface self-review

Review your own PR the way the reviewer will:

1. **The diff** — token usage, naming, dead code, test coverage.
2. **The preview environment** — the MRT URL on your branch.
3. **Figma, side by side** — at mobile *and* desktop. Layout bugs are invisible in a diff and
   invisible to every automated gate.

### Local CodeRabbit

```bash
coderabbit auth status
cr review --light --base develop
```

Required by AGENTS.md, verified by nothing. Use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth
fixing now or leaving for the PR review — but the review must actually run.

### Self-check

- [ ] `tsc`, `lint`, `test`, `audit:tokens`, `build` all clean
- [ ] Story exists, with `play` if there's interactive behaviour
- [ ] Test exists if there's branching or event wiring
- [ ] No raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment
- [ ] No bare token key on a sizing or typography prop
- [ ] Recipe namespaced and registered in `theme/components/index.ts`
- [ ] Keyboard-operable, focus visible, names on all controls, 24×24 targets
- [ ] Compared against Figma at mobile and desktop
- [ ] Jira URL in the PR body (the Forge app isn't installed — nothing does this for you)
- [ ] Protection-tier block filled honestly
- [ ] No `Co-Authored-By` trailer

### ⚠️ Read the check *history*, not the head SHA

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** `detect-changes` diffs
`since_last_remote_commit`, so a final docs-only commit can flip both required checks to green
even if an earlier push failed them. This happened on PR #59 — a 93-commit PR became
merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.

Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

## 10. Responding to a CodeRabbit review

**Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit's learning picks up patterns
from PR conversation. Silence teaches it nothing; a fix commit with no reply doesn't count.

- **Fixed** → a short reply confirming it, referencing the commit.
- **Not fixing** → explain *which specific rule or doc* justifies it, so the same pattern gets
  recognised next time instead of re-flagged.

Nothing enforces this: `requiresConversationResolution` is `false` on all three protected
branches, so a PR merges with every thread unanswered.

### What the declines on PR #59 established

These encode more project convention than the fixes did:

- **Only four files are true absolutes** — `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
  `worker/main.js`. Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named
  absolutes is.
- **Never argue "the rationale isn't engaged"** against unconditionally-worded text. That's an
  over-read, and it was conceded as one.
- **An incidental Tier 1 edit that *could* be split out *should* be.** Declining on mootness is
  the weak position.
- **Fixing a bug in one component doesn't license touching its neighbours** (Hard Rule #5) —
  even a confirmed real bug, if it's pre-existing and out of scope. The systemic fix is a lint
  rule with its own story.
- **Never accept CodeRabbit's offer to open a GitHub issue.** This project tracks in Jira; a
  GitHub issue is a parallel tracker nobody watches.
- **When a repo rule is stated unconditionally, conform even for a provable no-op** — and add
  an inline comment saying so, so the next reader doesn't hunt for phantom state.
- **Cite the PRD line before you cite it.** A wrong citation in a decline poisons CodeRabbit's
  learning store and has to be retracted in-thread, not silently amended in a later commit.

### Two switches that silence it invisibly

`chore(deps)` or `dependabot` **in the PR title** disables CodeRabbit entirely — title-matched,
not author-matched. So does draft status. Neither shows as a failing check; it just goes quiet.

## 11. Hard stops

1. Never work on `develop` or `main`.
2. Never modify a Tier 1 file without it being named in the prompt and owner approval confirmed.
3. Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`.
4. Never modify `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` — absolute,
   no exception.
5. Never refactor upward. Fixing a component doesn't mean touching the hook it calls.
6. Never rename or move a shared hook or component.
7. Never add or remove packages without Integration approval. When approved, `npm install` —
   don't hand-edit `package.json`.
8. Never modify test configuration.
9. Never delete files without being explicitly asked.
10. Never touch more than one protection tier in a change without confirming scope.
11. Never commit, push, or open a PR without an explicit request in the current prompt.
    Resuming from a summary or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit.

### Shared shell needs coordination

`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`,
`uiCopyProvider/`, `routes.tsx` are Tier 2 Global Shell, owned by **both** squads. Coordinate
before touching.

⚠️ **`.claude/rules/` is documentation; `CODEOWNERS` is configuration.** When you want to know
what will actually block a merge, read `CODEOWNERS`. It has **no catch-all rule**, so a path
absent from it needs no code-owner review regardless of what any rules file says. `squadA.md`
and `squadB.md` are six weeks stale and contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership — CODEOWNERS
says Squad B and is the one that enforces.

## 12. Performance

LCP ≤ **2s at p75 mobile**. Not a polish pass.

- **Images** — always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-resolution
  image at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting** — dynamic `import()` for anything heavy not needed on first render.
- **Data fetching** — request only the fields you need; parallelise. Waterfalls are not
  acceptable.
- **Third-party** — nothing loads before consent, and nothing consent-gated may block LCP. Use
  `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection.
- **Bundle** — `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB, enforced by `bundlesize`.

⚠️ **No CSS budget exists.** `projectState.md`'s "main.css < 50 kB" was never implemented. CSS
growth is currently ungated in both directions.

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit                 # gated nowhere — run it yourself
npm run lint                     # gated nowhere
npm run test                     # Vitest — required check on develop
npm run audit:tokens             # gated nowhere; 19 violations outstanding
npm run build
cr review --light --base develop
```

`npm start` — **do not run.** Ask for a restart if needed.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Design tokens (Tier 1) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
| Registered recipes | `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` |
| Co-located recipe | `<component>/<name>.css.ts` |
| Zimmermann components | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` |
| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons` |
| Shared types | `overrides/app/types/` |

**Icons:** never import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is
missing from the overrides set, ask — don't substitute a visually similar one.
(`header/index.tsx:60` currently violates this.)

### The eight things people get wrong most

1. A bare token key on a **sizing** prop — `width: 'xl'` = 576px.
2. A recipe not namespaced, silently merging into a base SFCC recipe.
3. A recipe not registered — runtime throw on destructuring.
4. A base-path import of an already-overridden component — renders the base version in
   Storybook and Vitest.
5. `padding: 'xs 0'` — compound values never tokenise.
6. A raw literal with no `provisional`/`pending` comment.
7. Assuming the component is broken when the **data doesn't exist on that tier**.
8. Reading a PR's head-SHA checks as green when they're actually `skipping`.

  every merge, not just before.

  things that break — `testing.md:87`'s `@storybook/test`, `testing.md:100`'s missing portal
  carve-out. Check the rule against the installed package before contorting the code.

### Three-surface self-review

Review your own PR the way the reviewer will:

1. **The diff** — token usage, naming, dead code, test coverage.
2. **The preview environment** — the MRT URL on your branch.
3. **Figma, side by side** — at mobile *and* desktop. Layout bugs are invisible in a diff and
   invisible to every automated gate.

### Local CodeRabbit

```bash
coderabbit auth status
cr review --light --base develop
```

Required by AGENTS.md, verified by nothing. Use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth
fixing now or leaving for the PR review — but the review must actually run.

### Self-check

- [ ] `tsc`, `lint`, `test`, `audit:tokens`, `build` all clean
- [ ] Story exists, with `play` if there's interactive behaviour
- [ ] Test exists if there's branching or event wiring
- [ ] No raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment
- [ ] No bare token key on a sizing or typography prop
- [ ] Recipe namespaced and registered in `theme/components/index.ts`
- [ ] Keyboard-operable, focus visible, names on all controls, 24×24 targets
- [ ] Compared against Figma at mobile and desktop
- [ ] Jira URL in the PR body (the Forge app isn't installed — nothing does this for you)
- [ ] Protection-tier block filled honestly
- [ ] No `Co-Authored-By` trailer

### ⚠️ Read the check *history*, not the head SHA

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** `detect-changes` diffs
`since_last_remote_commit`, so a final docs-only commit can flip both required checks to green
even if an earlier push failed them. This happened on PR #59 — a 93-commit PR became
merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.

Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

---

## 10. Responding to a CodeRabbit review

**Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit's learning picks up patterns
from PR conversation. Silence teaches it nothing; a fix commit with no reply doesn't count.

- **Fixed** → a short reply confirming it, referencing the commit.
- **Not fixing** → explain *which specific rule or doc* justifies it, so the same pattern gets
  recognised next time instead of re-flagged.

Nothing enforces this: `requiresConversationResolution` is `false` on all three protected
branches, so a PR merges with every thread unanswered.

### What the declines on PR #59 established

These encode more project convention than the fixes did:

- **Only four files are true absolutes** — `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
  `worker/main.js`. Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named
  absolutes is.
- **Never argue "the rationale isn't engaged"** against unconditionally-worded text. That's an
  over-read, and it was conceded as one.
- **An incidental Tier 1 edit that *could* be split out *should* be.** Declining on mootness is
  the weak position.
- **Fixing a bug in one component doesn't license touching its neighbours** (Hard Rule #5) —
  even a confirmed real bug, if it's pre-existing and out of scope. The systemic fix is a lint
  rule with its own story.
- **Never accept CodeRabbit's offer to open a GitHub issue.** This project tracks in Jira; a
  GitHub issue is a parallel tracker nobody watches.
- **When a repo rule is stated unconditionally, conform even for a provable no-op** — and add
  an inline comment saying so, so the next reader doesn't hunt for phantom state.
- **Cite the PRD line before you cite it.** A wrong citation in a decline poisons CodeRabbit's
  learning store and has to be retracted in-thread, not silently amended in a later commit.

not author-matched. So does draft status. Neither shows as a failing check; it just goes quiet.

1. Never work on `develop` or `main`.
2. Never modify a Tier 1 file without it being named in the prompt and owner approval confirmed.
3. Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`.
4. Never modify `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` — absolute,
   no exception.
5. Never refactor upward. Fixing a component doesn't mean touching the hook it calls.
6. Never rename or move a shared hook or component.
7. Never add or remove packages without Integration approval. When approved, `npm install` —
   don't hand-edit `package.json`.
8. Never modify test configuration.
9. Never delete files without being explicitly asked.
10. Never touch more than one protection tier in a change without confirming scope.
11. Never commit, push, or open a PR without an explicit request in the current prompt.
    Resuming from a summary or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit.

### Shared shell needs coordination

`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`,

- **Code splitting** — dynamic `import()` for anything heavy not needed on first render.

# UI Build — Knowledge & Context

How UI actually gets built and verified in this codebase: Salesforce PWA Kit v10 slim
`overrides/`, Chakra UI v2.7.0, Storybook 10, Zimmermann design tokens.

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Every claim below was
re-verified against the live toolchain and working tree on **22 August 2026** rather than taken on
trust from where it was first learned. Where a widely-repeated belief turned out to be wrong, the
correction is marked **[CORRECTED]**.

---

## 1. How a value resolves

The one-way chain. Each layer may read the one above it, never the reverse:

```
theme/foundation/*.ts            source values, designer-owned — you do not add tokens here
   |
theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts   DERIVED output, emits --zimm-* onto :root — never hand-edit
   |
theme/components/<name>.ts       recipes, consuming var(--zimm-*)
   |
component JSX                    textStyle + semantic tokens only
```

### The registration reality

`theme/index.ts` registers **`borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space`,
`textStyles`** and nothing else. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are absent.
Measured by bundling the live theme and evaluating `css(...)(toCSSVar(theme))`:

```
padding:   'xs 0'   ->  {"padding": "xs 0"}                   // verbatim -> browser DROPS it
width:     'xl'     ->  {"width": "var(--chakra-sizes-xl)"}   // 36rem, not space.xl's 1.5rem
fontSize:  'l'      ->  {"fontSize": "l"}                     // no such key -> DROPPED
textStyle: 'footer' ->  6 resolved literals, zero var()
```

| Prop family | Resolves through | Bare scale key |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` `top/right/bottom/left` | `theme.space` (registered) | **Correct** |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` (NOT registered) | **8x-112x wrong, or dropped** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | `theme.fontSizes` etc. (NOT registered) | Wrong value, or dropped |

Worst measured case: `3xs`, intended as 2px, emits **224px**. `s`/`m`/`l` have no Chakra `sizes`
key at all, so those declarations vanish silently rather than blowing up.

**This is the most dangerous thing in the styling layer, because the syntax is identical.**
`padding: 'xl'` is correct; `width: 'xl'` is a catastrophe. On sizing and typography props, always
the CSS var: `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`.

Live instance still in the tree: `components/header/index.tsx:302` ships `fontSize="l"`, which
emits nothing.

### textStyle can never emit a var, and what follows from that

`zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse would be a circular import.
`textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build time. **This is correct
behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw
literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.**

**The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax.** Ask of any value: *is this typed
more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on syntax generates mostly noise.

### Value equality is not token equality

**[CORRECTED]** Three constants were once flagged as mirrors duplicating existing tokens. **All
three were false positives.** Rewriting `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` to `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` would
have been a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression** — that token is authored in **px**, which does not scale
under zoom — plus a numeric-alias violation, and there is no valid named token in the gap (the
scale jumps 2.5rem to 4rem).

Before "fixing" an apparent duplicate, gate it on three checks:

1. **Same unit?** rem and px are not interchangeable; rem is required wherever text or spacing must
   scale under zoom.
2. **Same semantic scale?** A coincidental numeric match is not a relationship.
3. **Is the target permitted?** `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases are class-only; naming one from
   a recipe is itself a violation.

Known numeric-alias violations: `listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84` and `header.ts:59`. Match them with
`var(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+)` — a bare `[0-9]` also matches `3xs` and inflates the count.

### Units

`rem` for anything that must scale with root font size or zoom (type, spacing). `px` only for
hairline geometry that must *not* scale: border widths, focus-ring offsets. `em` only for
breakpoints.

---

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

**`extendTheme` deep-merges, so namespace every recipe.** SFCC ships its own `Footer` recipe.
Naming ours `Footer` merged into it: copyright rendered 14px instead of 10px, the subscribe heading
lost its 24px gap. The mechanism is ordering — an existing key is overwritten *in place*, a **new**
key is appended **last**, so your `margin: 0` shorthand lands after the base's `marginBottom` and
wipes it. Hence `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmNavItem`.

**A recipe unit test cannot catch this.** In isolation Chakra emitted the correct order; the
collision only appears merged. Intentional merges are allowlisted in `recipeGuards.test.ts`:
`Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu`.

**Compound values are never tokenised.** Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` ships verbatim and the browser discards it. Use axis props.

**Shorthand after longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` silently kills it. Use
`paddingInline`.

**`IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a style prop**, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:` in
your recipe size is discarded. Size it with `minW`/`minH`.

**Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Every new recipe goes into
`theme/components/index.ts`. Note the split: theme key is PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`), file is
camelCase (`zimmTextInput.ts`).

**`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap`** — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`.
An offline theme audit that skips that wrap passes for the wrong reason.

---

## 3. Component structure

**Placement, settled.** Design-system components live at:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/      zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/  zimmInputAction/
  organisms/  (does not exist yet)
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing: `generateRegistry.mjs` only scans that directory.

**Casing: three families, each correct in its own. Do not generalise between them.**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream exactly |

**Tier follows what the component's own template renders**, not visual size. Atom renders no other
component; molecule renders only atoms; organism renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a
prop does not count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom), and slotted children do not count.
Porting from the F2R library, the tier is already recorded as `composes: [...]` — use it.

**Styling surface: a theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not
co-located CSS. For a bespoke component wrapping a native element the `chakra()` factory is the
bridge — native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`. F2R `.styles.ts`
files using `.zimm-*` classes are good raw material: **convert them to a recipe, do not copy the
pattern**, and never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

The reasoning is worth keeping. A stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is derived output
at the *bottom* of the pipeline. Author there and you forfeit `textStyle`, the named `theme.space`
scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the theme drift guards. Not bad CSS, just the
wrong end of the chain.

**Data-fetching never lives in `components/`.** A component that owns its own fetching cannot be
reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched, story-mocked, or passed from a parent.

### Two API patterns worth copying

**Encode the a11y contract in the type.** `ZimmButton` uses a discriminated union where `label` is
required in both members and doubles as `aria-label` for the icon variant — an unlabelled icon
button is *unconstructible*.

**An affordance absent from the design spec is opt-in, defaulting off** (`clearable?: boolean`).
Adding it by default put two controls in one field.

### Do not trust the generated registry's tier column

`generateRegistry.mjs:122` hardcodes tier arrays duplicating `.claude/rules/`, lists no `ui-kits`
path, and `getTier()` defaults to `4 - Feature-local`. Every design-system atom is therefore
reported as Tier 4.

---

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three ways an override silently fails to take effect. Check all three before assuming your file is
live.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
imports in the real app build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases the package straight to `node_modules`
and `vitest.config.ts` does not touch it. So a base-path import of a component you *have*
overridden renders correctly in the app and renders the **unstyled base** in Storybook and Vitest.
Inside an override, import a sibling override by **relative path**.

**2. A relative re-export in a barrel is not rewritten.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` is
`export {Button} from './Button'` — relative, so the resolver never sees it. Counted: **208 base
files import the barrel, 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` therefore
intercepts **nothing**, which kills the otherwise-appealing "own the primitive layer and propagate
for free" strategy.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding `footer` does not reach `/checkout`,
because base `_app/index.jsx:484` is `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}`, and
`CheckoutFooter` resolves to `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` — a different module your
override does not shadow.

**The generalised check:** grep for who imports your path *and* for conditional renders of
alternates.

```bash
grep -rn "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

Worth knowing before estimating: `overrides/app/components/` holds only **seven** directories on
`develop`. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still base despite being referenced throughout the
rules files. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's worked example not
to exist yet.

---

## 5. Figma to code

### The node-type discriminator

This decides whether a delta is worth chasing, and it is not a fudge factor:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box** and are **directly comparable**, so a delta there
  is a genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was real; a blanket
  "it is just cap height" rule would have dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all at +7 after every real cause was removed was the heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` plus
4.5px padding gave 24/24/24/24/38 = 134, exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### Two files exist, so never cross-compare

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` is the design system; `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` is composed page states.
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three ways an override silently fails to take effect. Check all three before assuming your file is
live.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
imports in the real app build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases the package straight to `node_modules`
and `vitest.config.ts` does not touch it. So a base-path import of a component you *have*
overridden renders correctly in the app and renders the **unstyled base** in Storybook and Vitest.
Inside an override, import a sibling override by **relative path**.

**2. A relative re-export in a barrel is not rewritten.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` is
`export {Button} from './Button'` — relative, so the resolver never sees it. Counted: **208 base
files import the barrel, 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` therefore
intercepts **nothing**, which kills the otherwise-appealing "own the primitive layer and propagate
for free" strategy.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding `footer` does not reach `/checkout`,
because base `_app/index.jsx:484` is `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}`, and
`CheckoutFooter` resolves to `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` — a different module your
override does not shadow.

**The generalised check:** grep for who imports your path *and* for conditional renders of
alternates.

```bash
grep -rn "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

Worth knowing before estimating: `overrides/app/components/` holds only **seven** directories on
`develop`. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still base despite being referenced throughout the
rules files. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's worked example not
to exist yet.

## 5. Figma to code

### The node-type discriminator

This decides whether a delta is worth chasing, and it is not a fudge factor:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,

  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.

4.5px padding gave 24/24/24/24/38 = 134, exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

## 6. Layout mechanics

Each cost real debugging time and none is obvious from a screenshot.

- **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content` resolves
  to the widest unbreakable run.
- **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** Derive height from
  `lineHeight` plus padding instead.
- **Inline descender leak:** a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds roughly 1.5-2px per
  row via the line-box strut. Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`.
- **Gap ownership.** If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, do not reproduce it as
  a sibling in a gapped flex container — you inherit a gap the design does not have. Give the gap to
  the heading (`marginBottom`) rather than the column.
- **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the words
  break instead.
- **A non-breaking space is the tool for controlling a wrap point** when no column cap can satisfy
  two constraints at once. Always write it as the escape `\u00A0`, never as a literal NBSP
  byte — a literal one is invisible in review and in a diff.

## 7. Building against absent data

Most integrations land later and UI work is not blocked on them. Three patterns exist; only the
first is correct.

**(1) Guard, then render inert but perceivable — correct.** No `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing
promises an action the app cannot perform (avoiding the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance) — but
**labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so assistive tech still announces the channel exists (avoiding the
1.1.1 information loss). Switch to the live branch the moment a real destination arrives.

**(2) Fallback to empty string — a layout bug.** `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that keeps
its margins; measured as a roughly 64px void.

**(3) Silent element swap — the worst.** Link-to-button when href validation fails hands the user a
control that looks identical and does nothing. It is the only one of the three that actively lies.

Fix (2) and (3) **at the atom**, not the call site: one change covers every consumer.

**Never "render nothing."** A missing component reads as a defect to anyone reviewing the design
surface, and the links cannot be tested at all.

### Guarding hrefs

Any href from CMS or fixture data goes through the shared guard. The non-obvious part: the WHATWG
URL parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space characters and removes tab, LF and CR **before**
parsing, so a browser reads a backslash-prefixed path as protocol-relative. A regex without
backslash and control-character handling has a live bypass — exactly the gap that shipped. Normalise
first, then test:

```ts
/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
const normalise = (href: string) =>
  href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
```

A space-prefixed path stays allowed on purpose: a space is percent-encoded by the browser and
cannot become protocol-relative.

## 8. Accessibility patterns

The criteria that recur, and what each actually demanded:

- **2.5.8 Target size (24px min)** — controls measured 16x16 and had to become 24x24. On an
  `IconButton`, size via `minW`/`minH`; `p:` is discarded (section 2).
- **2.4.7 Focus visible** — the ring belongs in the recipe's `_focusVisible` so every consumer
  inherits it. Note **programmatic `.focus()` does not match `:focus-visible`** in Chromium, so a
  test that focuses by script reports no ring even when keyboard focus shows one. Drive it with a
  real `Tab`.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must contain the visible label.
- **3.2.5, new-window announcement** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and
  a suffix in its accessible name.
- **1.1.1 vs 2.4.4/3.2.4** — the tension behind pattern (1): `aria-hidden` loses information, a
  fake affordance lies. Labelled-and-inert satisfies both.
- **1.4.4 Resize text** — why spacing and type are authored in `rem`, and why a px-authored token
  is not a valid substitute for a rem literal (section 1).

**Interaction state belongs in the recipe** (`_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`), never
in `useState`. React state looks identical in a screenshot but is dead until hydration, sticky on
touch, and unstylable by the theme.
