## 9. Verification: what actually proves anything

### The integrity principle

> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
> never made to fail on purpose.

That one sentence explains 22 catalogued instances of a green check proving nothing. The standard
that follows: **a check must be made to fail deliberately before its pass counts.**

**Copy the non-vacuity meta-test.** `recipeGuards.test.ts` asserts its own inputs are non-empty —
*"without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green."* All four of its guards
stayed green with `components` stubbed to an empty object until that was added.

**Watch for a green test that encodes a bug as correct.** "contact icons are not focusable" passed
because there were no hrefs to focus; wiring them correctly *dropped* the suite to 19/20. "locale
button inert" was green whether the control was inert by omission or genuinely disabled. If a test
would pass equally on the broken and the fixed version, it asserts nothing.

**Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient.** A focus trap was mutation-tested in both wrap
directions and still let focus escape the `aria-modal` dialog when focus arrived from outside the
focusable set. Aim for orthogonal matrices where each mutation kills exactly one assertion, plus
deliberate false-positive controls.

### Harness reality

- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results
  uninterpretable because the baseline itself failed.
- **Vitest does not run `play` functions.** A story `play` is not unit coverage.
- **Every jsdom rect is 0**, so layout assertions there are meaningless.
- **jsdom always provides `window`**, so an SSR branch needs a node test environment or every case
  takes the browser path.
- **`extendTheme` leaves `__cssMap` empty** — wrap with `toCSSVar` or the assertion is vacuous.

### What is and is not gated

**[CORRECTED] a11y IS gated.** The widely-repeated conclusion that it was not ("no
`.storybook/test-runner.js`") was Storybook 8 knowledge. With what is installed —
`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`, `addon-a11y@10.4.6`, `axe-core@4.11.4` — the runner reads
`parameters.a11y.test` and rejects on `"error"`, which `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets. No
`test-runner.js` is needed. **Do not delete that block.** It has never been made to fail on
purpose, so it is unproven rather than absent.

**Gated nowhere:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, any CSS bundle budget. `npm run lint`
currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing errors and CI never notices. `bundlesize` does not run on
PRs to `develop`.

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** `detect-changes` uses
`since_last_remote_commit: true`, so a final push touching only files outside every allow-list
leaves *required* suites showing `skipping` while the PR stays mergeable — zero test evidence on the
head SHA. Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

**`.claude/rules/testing.md:87` prescribes `@storybook/test`, which is not installed.** Storybook 10
moved it to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks.

### The gap no tool covers

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving to 36rem blew
contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`, `eslint`,
`vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only rendering the page beside Figma
found it. Budget for that pass; nothing upstream of it will save you.

# UI Build — Knowledge & Context

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Those live in
`fedLead-playbook.md` (the role) and `fedBuild-manual.md` (the procedure).

Every claim here was measured against the installed toolchain, not inherited from an
earlier note. Beliefs that turned out to be wrong are marked **[CORRECTED]** and the
correction is kept visible rather than silently overwritten — a claim that was confidently
wrong once is worth flagging so it isn't re-derived.

*Re-verified 2026-08-25 against `develop` @ `8362b3c` (PR #59 merged) with
`feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info` checked out.*

---

## 1. How a value resolves

### The pipeline is one-way

```
theme/foundation/*.ts   ← source of truth (Tier 1)
        ↓
zimmTokens.ts           ← DERIVED. Never hand-edit.
        ↓
--zimm-* CSS custom properties
        ↓
recipes: <name>.css.ts / theme/components/*.ts
        ↓
component JSX
```

`zimmTokens.ts` imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/
`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid` from their owning files rather than
retyping values. The only literals left in it are 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with
no named-scale equivalent.

**A Tier 1 comment is wrong about those 7.** `theme/index.ts:47` says the 15 numeric aliases
*"are duplicates of the named scale."* `overrideStyling.md:83-85` says 7 of them are not, and
`overrideStyling.md` is right: `025` (1px), `700` (28px), `1100` (44px), `1200` (48px),
`1300` (52px), `3500` (140px), `4500` (180px) are hardcoded in `zimmTokens.ts`; the other 8
derive from `spacing`.

### The registration reality — this is the one that breaks layouts

`theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only** (line 56). `sizes`,
`fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are deliberately **not** registered, because
registering them would restyle the base retail-react-app at ~199 call sites.

| Prop family | Reads | Bare key like `'xl'` |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | correct |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ not registered | **falls through to Chakra's defaults** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | ❌ not registered | wrong value, or nothing |

Measured blow-up range: **8×–112×**. `width: 'xl'` resolves through `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem
= **576px** — that shipped, blew the footer contact icons to 576px, and destroyed the layout
on every page. Worse: `s`, `m`, `l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are dropped entirely and silently.

Typography has the same twin. `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was intended;
`fontSize: '4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` has `fontSize="l"`,
which emits nothing. Pre-existing, out of scope for every PR that has touched that file since.
`recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot reach it — it walks the registered recipe map only, and this is
a JSX prop. Its own `SCOPE:` note says so.

**The rule:** on a sizing or typography prop, always the CSS var —
`width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`. Spacing props are fine with bare keys as
far as *correctness* goes; house style is a separate question, below.

### [CORRECTED] `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now required, not a smell

An earlier revision of this document said component JSX should use `textStyle` plus semantic
token strings (`color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`), and that seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was
a signal to look closer. **That is inverted from the current rule and following it now fails
review.**

`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 and `css.md` both state it plainly:

```tsx
// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ the raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

The stated reason is **house style, not correctness**: a bare key resolves to the identical
value on a registered scale, but it forces a reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s
registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. A `var()` reference is
unambiguous at every call site.

`textStyle` is the one legitimate bare key — there is no `var()` for the composite expansion,
only for its individual pieces.

**What survives from the old advice, and is still the main point:** brand values mostly should
not be in JSX at all. Measured on `develop` 2026-08-25 — `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18
recipe files** (14 co-located `<name>.css.ts` + 4 `theme/components/*.ts`) and in exactly
**one** component `.tsx`: `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`, a conditional
`paddingLeft` that no Chakra prop expresses. So the practice is: type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine prop-system gap.

**Live violations right now:** `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and
`zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23` both use `color="text.default"`.

### The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax

Ask of any value: *is this typed more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on
syntax generates mostly noise.

PR #56 reduced `foundation/`'s hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 — **173 were duplicates**,
the same `24px` appearing in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Two later PRs
recreated that duplication one layer up without noticing: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times; PR #55 added `cssVars.ts`, 241 lines mirroring
`zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered text
styles. It was removed — 245 lines, 53 references across 8 files.

Both misreads passed CodeRabbit. It confirmed every correctness finding and raised **zero**
architecture findings.

### Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with root font-size or browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) —
  type and spacing. Sub-pixel letter-spacing values keep a trailing `// -0.12px` comment for
  traceability, since they don't round to clean rem.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`, deliberate so media queries shift with zoom)
  and other genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

---

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

Seven mechanisms. None produces an error, a warning, or a failing type-check.

**1. `extendTheme` deep-merges — it does not replace.** A recipe named `Footer` merges into
base SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it, inheriting parts you never wrote. Namespace
everything: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this with
`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate; anything
else must be namespaced.

**2. A recipe unit test cannot catch the merge.** `extendTheme` does **not** populate
`theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. So a direct `css()(theme)`
assertion in Vitest passes vacuously against an unmerged object.

**3. Compound values never tokenise.** Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Use axis props
(`paddingInline`, `paddingBlock`).

**4. A shorthand declared after a longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock`
wipes it. Order matters; prefer the axis props throughout.

**5. `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"`.** Any padding you pass is overwritten.

**6. Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the
string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — so co-location is free, but the
key must be in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**7. Breakpoint tokens conflict with Chakra's.** `BP.desktop` is 64em; Chakra's `lg` is 62em
and `xl` is 80em. A responsive array silently steps at the wrong width. Write explicit media
queries:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand also puts a bare token key at every step, and the guard flags all four.

---

## 3. Component structure

### Placement — settled

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.

**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.

### Tier is by composition, not visual size

Read it off the imports, not the DOM:

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
  come from the caller).
- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
  + local validation state.
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
  owns the subscribe state machine.

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
children don't count.

**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.

### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always

Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
string key, so this is purely organisational.

The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.

**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).

`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.

### No data-fetching in `components/`

Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.

**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,

read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for
every consumer regardless of route, not anything that varies per page.

**Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades:
`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, one line, renders with zero setup. **`useIntl`
throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the base SFCC `_app`,
not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer
must wrap it.

Three silent failure modes. In each, the override compiles, resolves, and never runs.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` in `package.json` redirects

`.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`
doesn't touch it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden component builds correctly in
the shipped app and silently renders the **unstyled base version** in Storybook and Vitest —
the story looks like it's exercising your override and isn't.

(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path.

**2. A relative barrel re-export is not rewritten.** The attractive play — override

## 6. Layout mechanics

Six mechanisms, each with its fix.

1. **Wrapped-element width** — a wrapper shrinks to content unless told otherwise.
2. **`minHeight` + centring** — reserves space without collapsing when empty.
3. **Inline descender leak** — an inline element's line box includes descender space; use
   `display: block` or set `lineHeight` explicitly.
4. **Gap ownership** — the parent owns the gap, never the child's margin. Two owners drift.
5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking** — the words break instead.
6. **NBSP as ` `** — a literal non-breaking space in source is invisible to review and
   survives reformatting unpredictably.

## 7. Building against absent data

### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — the box collapses and everything shifts.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

# FED Lead Playbook

**Derived from:** the two "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" sessions
**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026
**Companions:** [fedBuild-manual.md](./fedBuild-manual.md) (the developer-facing half — how to build) · [componentStories-BA-guide.md](./componentStories-BA-guide.md) (the BA-facing version) · [pr52-pr55-findings.md](./pr52-pr55-findings.md) (worked example of Play 5 applied to two live PRs) · `.docs/temp/{componentStoryReview,meeting2Prep,meeting2Analysis}.md` (the underlying analysis)
**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` in-repo — if this playbook and that file disagree, it wins.

Purpose: the two sessions put sixteen things on your desk without saying when or how any of them get done. This turns that into a rhythm, a set of repeatable plays, and the specific mechanics for each.

---

## 1. The mandate, consolidated

What the sessions actually assigned you:

| # | Responsibility | From |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Own dependency discovery during refinement | M1 — the strongest expectation raised |
| 2 | Protect Salesforce / PWA Kit reuse; challenge "let's build this" | M1 |
| 3 | Own component governance — prevent duplicate Buttons, Links, utilities | M1 |
| 4 | Strengthen FE PR review criteria | M1 |
| 5 | Improve estimation accuracy — surface hidden work before planning | M1 (Jasmijn, repeatedly) |
| 6 | Embed accessibility in component stories, not as follow-up | M1 + M2 |
| 7 | Follow up design-system gaps with Kiera / design owners | M1 |
| 8 | Define the atoms governance model + a refinement checklist | M1 (strategic) |
| 9 | Component completeness — all variants designed upfront | M2 |
| 10 | Define a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components | M2 |
| 11 | Ensure components gracefully handle optional fields | M2 |
| 12 | Document accessibility expectations component-by-component | M2 |
| 13 | Own page-level validation — visual, responsive, integration, design parity | M2 |
| 14 | Push back where requirements are unclear before sizing | M2 |
| 15 | Support incremental assembly (build → drop in → verify) | M2 |
| 16 | Separate component-build effort from page-composition effort in estimates | M2 |

**The through-line, in Tim's words:** *"FED leadership needs to identify what already exists before the team commits to building something new."*

**The one to resist as stated.** #1 makes you a serial gate across both squads' refinement sessions. It won't scale and it will slip. Play 1 handles this by moving the lookup to where the story is drafted and keeping only the judgement calls for yourself.

### The quality bar this all serves

Everything below is calibrated to one number. **The SOW allows no more than 10 defects, and no Sev3.**

Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination means the usual
trade — ship it, fix it in QA — is not available here. A visual defect that would be a shrug on another
project consumes part of a very small budget.

Three consequences to plan around rather than discover:

- **Vigilance is the job, not an overhead on the job.** Be as vigilant as possible, on every PR.
- **Budget real time for checking.** A proper pass over a UI PR — preview environment, Figma, tokens,
  states, responsive — is **an hour or more**. Treat that as the cost of the review, not as slippage.
- **Do as much as we can and flag the rest.** Where design is missing, ambiguous or contradictory, the
  answer is to raise it, not to invent a value. An invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system
  divergence.

---

## 2. Your operating rhythm

Sixteen responsibilities, four moments. Everything below hangs off this.

| When | Plays | Time |
|---|---|---|
| **Story drafting** (BA-initiated, async) | 1 — reuse & dependency check | Async, minutes per story |
| **Refinement** (per story) | 1, 3, 9, 14 — dependencies, variants, push-back | In the session |
| **Pre-sprint-planning** (weekly) | 2 — estimation validation | ~30 min |
| **PR review** (continuous) | 5 — the human-only checks | Per PR |
| **Design review** (weekly, with Kiera) | 6 — design-system gaps | Standing slot |

Two standing items that don't fit a cadence: the **renderer contract** (Play 4, once per Contentful component) and **page-level validation** (Play 7, once per page assembly).

---

## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

*Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8*

### The ladder (agreed in M1)

```
Salesforce / PWA Kit capability
        ↓  (nothing fits)
Existing shared component in overrides/
        ↓  (nothing fits)
Existing pattern
        ↓  (nothing fits)
New implementation  ← justify this out loud
```

### Where to actually look

| Question | Source |
|---|---|
| Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change |
| Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` |
| Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` |
| What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` |

The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below).

### Worked examples, already verified

| Ask | What already exists |
|---|---|
| Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test |
| Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant |
| Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` |
| Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` |

Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration.

### Override-first — why the second rung is where the value is

The ladder says "reuse before build". The stronger version, and the one to hold the line on:
**default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.**

The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override
`product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle
handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to be
re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points.

There's a second-order effect worth naming in refinement. PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports
transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base components already import means the whole base
template inherits your version** — no call sites touched. A bespoke component in a new folder reaches only
the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same visual result on the page you're building; very
different coverage across the site.

⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel
(`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from
'./Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import
that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>/` intercepts
nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not
an interception point. See "Two component families" below.

So the question in review isn't only "did you reuse?" but **"is this an override, and if not, why not?"**

**In flight, and relevant:** Han is extending the registry generator to account for the `shared/` folder
as well, and is building the override-first approach into the F2R workflow — so the default lands in the
tooling rather than depending on everyone remembering it. Worth tracking; it removes work from Play 1.

### The hidden cost to name every time

If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work:

1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/`
2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker
5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base**
6. Then build; remove markers

It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly.

### Making this scale (the fix for #1)

Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093:

> *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."*

That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement:

- **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?**
- **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?**

### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8)

The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model:

- A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`.
- **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories.
- The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer.

Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four.

### The atoms governance model — decided (closes #8)

Three developers independently inferred three different answers from the same rules file, so this is now
written down. Both halves are settled; the developer-facing version is in the FED Build Manual §3.

**Where they live, and what they're called**

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelName>/index.tsx
```

**camelCase, one folder per component.** These are Zimmermann-authored, so `conventions.md`'s default
applies; the kebab-case rule is scoped to files *mirroring a base Salesforce file*, and no
`@salesforce/…/zimm-button` exists to mirror. It also satisfies `components.md`'s named-export-matches-folder
rule. Precedents: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`.

Three casings coexist and each is right in its own family — worth stating in review, because generalising
from one to another is the mistake people make:

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path |
| ui-kit component | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | Zimmermann-authored — the default |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own casing |

**Tiering** is by what the component's own template renders — atom renders nothing, molecule renders only
atoms, organism renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count; slotted children
don't count. Tier follows composition, not pixel size. The F2R contract already records this as
`composes: [...]` and machine-checks it in `02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs`, so **use the contract's
tier rather than re-deriving it in refinement.**

**The styling surface: a theme recipe, always.**

| Case | Surface |
|---|---|
| It **is** a Chakra component | `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe; `variant`/`size` resolve automatically |
| **Bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | Recipe + register + `useMultiStyleConfig` + `chakra()` factory |
| Static, non-interactive, heavily reused | `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` |
| Nothing else fits | `sx`, then co-located `.scss` — last resort |

`theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` is the worked example for the bespoke case. The `chakra()` factory is
what makes it possible to style a native element from a recipe — that was the missing piece people kept
hitting.

**The argument to use when someone proposes co-located CSS instead** (and it will come up, because plain
CSS handles `:hover` perfectly well): a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is *derived output*.
Authoring there forfeits `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive
arrays and the 125 drift-guard tests. It's not bad CSS — it's the wrong end of the token pipeline.

---

## Play 2 — Estimation validation

*Covers responsibilities 5, 16*

Run this before sprint planning, not in it.

### The re-baseline to communicate once

M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence:

- **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper.
- **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.**

Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch.

If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly.

### Split the two kinds of effort (#16)

| Component build | Page composition |
|---|---|
| Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration |
| Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing |
| Storybook + tests | Visual validation |
| Sized as build work | Sized as validation work |

Don't let them be estimated with the same scale.

### Challenge list

## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

*Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8*

### The ladder (agreed in M1)

```
Salesforce / PWA Kit capability
        ↓  (nothing fits)
Existing shared component in overrides/
        ↓  (nothing fits)
Existing pattern
        ↓  (nothing fits)
New implementation  ← justify this out loud
```

### Where to actually look

| Question | Source |
|---|---|
| Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change |
| Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` |
| Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` |
| What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` |

The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below).

### Worked examples, already verified

| Ask | What already exists |
|---|---|
| Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test |
| Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant |
| Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` |
| Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` |

Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration.

### Override-first — why the second rung is where the value is

The ladder says "reuse before build". The stronger version, and the one to hold the line on:
**default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.**

The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override
`product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle
handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to be
re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points.

There's a second-order effect worth naming in refinement. PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports
transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base components already import means the whole base
template inherits your version** — no call sites touched. A bespoke component in a new folder reaches only
the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same visual result on the page you're building; very
different coverage across the site.

⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel
(`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from
'./Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import
that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>/` intercepts
nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not
an interception point. See "Two component families" below.

So the question in review isn't only "did you reuse?" but **"is this an override, and if not, why not?"**

**In flight, and relevant:** Han is extending the registry generator to account for the `shared/` folder
as well, and is building the override-first approach into the F2R workflow — so the default lands in the
tooling rather than depending on everyone remembering it. Worth tracking; it removes work from Play 1.

### The hidden cost to name every time

If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work:

1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/`
2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker
5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base**
6. Then build; remove markers

It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly.

### Making this scale (the fix for #1)

Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093:

> *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."*

That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement:

- **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?**
- **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?**

### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8)

The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model:

- A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`.
- **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories.
- The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer.

Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four.

### The atoms governance model — decided (closes #8)

Three developers independently inferred three different answers from the same rules file, so this is now
written down. Both halves are settled; the developer-facing version is in the FED Build Manual §3.

**Where they live, and what they're called**

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelName>/index.tsx
```

**camelCase, one folder per component.** These are Zimmermann-authored, so `conventions.md`'s default
applies; the kebab-case rule is scoped to files *mirroring a base Salesforce file*, and no
`@salesforce/…/zimm-button` exists to mirror. It also satisfies `components.md`'s named-export-matches-folder
rule. Precedents: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`.

Three casings coexist and each is right in its own family — worth stating in review, because generalising
from one to another is the mistake people make:

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path |
| ui-kit component | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | Zimmermann-authored — the default |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own casing |

**Tiering** is by what the component's own template renders — atom renders nothing, molecule renders only
atoms, organism renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count; slotted children
don't count. Tier follows composition, not pixel size. The F2R contract already records this as
`composes: [...]` and machine-checks it in `02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs`, so **use the contract's
tier rather than re-deriving it in refinement.**

**The styling surface: a theme recipe, always.**

| Case | Surface |
|---|---|
| It **is** a Chakra component | `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe; `variant`/`size` resolve automatically |
| **Bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | Recipe + register + `useMultiStyleConfig` + `chakra()` factory |
| Static, non-interactive, heavily reused | `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` |
| Nothing else fits | `sx`, then co-located `.scss` — last resort |

`theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` is the worked example for the bespoke case. The `chakra()` factory is
what makes it possible to style a native element from a recipe — that was the missing piece people kept
hitting.

**The argument to use when someone proposes co-located CSS instead** (and it will come up, because plain
CSS handles `:hover` perfectly well): a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is *derived output*.
Authoring there forfeits `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive
arrays and the 125 drift-guard tests. It's not bad CSS — it's the wrong end of the token pipeline.

---

## Play 2 — Estimation validation

*Covers responsibilities 5, 16*

Run this before sprint planning, not in it.

### The re-baseline to communicate once

M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence:

- **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper.
- **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.**

Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch.

If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly.

### Split the two kinds of effort (#16)

| Component build | Page composition |
|---|---|
| Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration |
| Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing |
| Storybook + tests | Visual validation |
| Sized as build work | Sized as validation work |

Don't let them be estimated with the same scale.

### Challenge list

For each story before it's sized:

- [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page?
- [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed?
- [ ] Storybook story accounted for?
- [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column)
- [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list?

One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. ### The distinction to hold | Kind | Examples | How it's built | |---|---|---| | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. ### Optional-field handling (#11) M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. --- ## Play 4 — The renderer contract *Covers responsibility 10* M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). --- ## Play 5 — PR review *Covers responsibility 4* The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it | Check | Enforced by | |---|---| | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | ### Not enforced — this is your list | Gap | Why it matters | |---|---| | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. ### Gate zero — does it actually build? **Check this before spending review attention on anything else.** A PR has already been opened on this project with a failing typecheck — missing type declarations that the branch itself had previously supplied and lost in a merge. Reviewing the design of code that doesn't compile wastes the expensive part of your day. ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # must be clean npm run lint # separate real errors from auto-fixable prettier noise npx vitest run ``` Two things worth knowing about this failure mode, because it will recur: - **A merge can silently delete a declaration.** When a branch merges `develop` and both sides touched the same ambient-types file, the merge can resolve to develop's version and drop what the branch added. It typechecks on neither side's intent and nobody notices until CI or a local build. - **It isn't always the author's mistake.** In that instance a second error came from following a repo rules file that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. Evaluate the rendered output against Figma deliberately, at the breakpoints the design defines. Anything that doesn't line up is either a build finding or a design gap — and separating those two is your call, not the developer's. ### Tokens and CSS — the highest-yield thing you check This is where divergence starts, it is not mechanically enforced, and both PRs currently in flight have drifted in different directions. Be deliberately vigilant here. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` is the authority. The hierarchy, in order: 1. `textStyle` for anything textual — **never** a raw `fontSize` 2. Are all design values tokens — and the *correct* tokens, in the correct layer? 4. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 5. Four times a conclusion reversed once the source was actually read, and each reversal would have shipped a wrong change.* ### Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision `f2r/02-design/specs/` files carry `` and a `Status: draft` header. They are **mechanical dumps of a Figma node**, not rulings. When the text-input spec had no `clearable` attribute, that meant the Figma component doesn't have one — not that the design system had ruled one out. Treating it as a ruling nearly deleted a control rather than making it opt-in. Same trap in the other direction: the spec *did* define `trailing-icon`, which settled a question two code comments had recorded backwards. ### A value in the codebase is not a spec until you find its source `header.ts` carried `width: min(597px, 60vw)` with a comment deriving 597 from 70 and the aspect ratio. Contrast the icon geometry: `327px`/`39px` cite Figma nodes in their comment, and the nodes check out. **The test:** can you name the node or the doc? If not, it's a guess someone typed, however confident the surrounding comment sounds. ### Ask for the node. It costs the designer thirty seconds. Four times on this build the answer came from reading a Figma node directly — the chevron geometry, the four chevron rotations, the site-map item heights, the subscribe heading binding. Each took one message. Each replaced a derivation I would otherwise have defended with arithmetic. Deriving is legitimate when the source *shows* the derivation — all four chevrons export an identical path, so Figma itself is rotating one glyph, and reproducing that is reading, not guessing. Deriving from "it's probably the same as the other one" is not. ### An audit that matches on value alone will produce confident nonsense A style-mirror check flagged three constants as duplicating existing tokens. - Behaviour when optional content is absent

**Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate.

### The one open item

M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter.

**Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled.

---

## Play 7 — Page-level validation

*Covers responsibilities 13, 15*

M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX.

### Where each part lands today

| Ask | Home |
|---|---|
| Assembled UX / integration | ⚠️ Playwright E2E — the `@area` **vocabulary** is `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations`, but only `@homepage` and `@checkout` are applied to any spec today. Five of the seven areas have no coverage at all |
| Performance | ✅ `lighthouserc.js` |
| Responsive behaviour | ⚠️ Partial — Playwright runs desktop + mobile Chrome, but asserts behaviour, not appearance |
| **Spacing / design fidelity / design parity** | ❌ **No automated home.** `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots from the Vitest budget |

**Name this rather than absorbing it.** Design-parity validation is currently manual visual QA. Either it's accepted as manual and the time is resourced, or it's a visual-regression tooling decision (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) — a new dependency and budget, which needs approval before anything is installed. An unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here.

Operational note: only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in the change-scoping config. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite.

Tim's build → drop-in → verify loop is well supported and costs nothing to adopt:

| Step | Support |
|---|---|
| Build in isolation | Storybook — mandatory story; `Contentful/` category explicitly allows mock CMS data |
| Make available to authors | `npm run generate:contentful` regenerates definitions; pre-commit keeps it in sync |
| Author drops it on a page | Studio Experiences — appears once annotated |
| Verify | `pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` routes exist |

**Caveat worth stating:** this loop only works for Studio Experiences components. Entry-driven ones are wired in code and aren't drag-and-droppable. Another reason the pattern question in Play 8 matters.

The devs work from the Figma links on the Jira card via the Figma MCP. That makes the link a **build

- the **BA** signs off AC written against a different frame,

content.content:
# FED Lead Playbook

**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026

The lead role: what you say, to whom, and when. Judgement and process, not procedure.

**Companions:** `fedBuild-manual.md` (how to build a component) · `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why
the machine behaves the way it does).

**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this file disagrees with it,
that file wins.

*This document absorbed `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (retired 25 Aug 2026). Its
durable operating principles are §3; its training-vehicle material — a Next.js/Tailwind stack
that isn't this one — was dropped.*

---

## 1. The mandate

Sixteen responsibilities landed across two Contentful-vs-PWA-Kit alignment meetings. They
reduce to two mandates:

- **M1 — Protect the build.** Reuse, conventions, review, accessibility, performance.
- **M2 — Protect the plan.** Estimation, scope, dependencies, escalation.

**The one to resist as stated:** being a serial refinement gate across both squads. It won't
scale and it will slip. Name that rather than absorbing it — an unresourced ask that quietly
becomes yours is the failure mode here.

### The quality bar this serves

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3**, for the whole project. Three consequences:

1. **Vigilance is the job**, not an overhead on it.
2. **Budget real time per UI PR** — an hour or more. That's the cost of the review, not
   slippage.
3. **Flag rather than invent.** A guessed value that ships is a defect with your name on it.

---

## 2. Operating rhythm

| Moment | Plays |
|---|---|
| Story drafting | 1, 3, 4 |
| Refinement | 1, 2, 8 |
| Pre-sprint planning | 2, 8 |
| PR review | 5, 5b, 6 |
| Weekly design review | 9 |

---

## 3. Principles

*Absorbed from the retired playbook. These are the parts that survived contact with the
codebase.*

### The quality ceiling is set by the human

An AI assistant has no standards of its own — the standards and the constraints are things you
supply. Its real value is making your assumptions visible faster, not making decisions.

### The dual mandate

You hold two hats and the failure mode is collapsing into one.

| | IC | Lead |
|---|---|---|
| Think | about the component | about the system |
| Ask | until the spec is unambiguous | until the *team's* spec is unambiguous |
| Decide | how to build it | whether it should be built now |
| Review | your own output hardest | the pattern, not the line |
| Protect | the build | the plan |
| Multiply | — | the highest-leverage thing you do |

**IC drift:** you're the only one who knows how something works. **Lead drift:** you haven't
written code in a week and your review comments are getting vaguer.

### Defeating agreeableness

An assistant that agrees with you is worth nothing. Four techniques that work:

- **Role framing** — "you are a reviewer whose job is to find what's wrong with this."
- **Steelman** — "give me the strongest argument *against* this approach."
- **Critique-first** — ask for the problems before asking for the solution.
- **Constraint injection** — name the constraint it must satisfy, so it can't hand-wave.

Make it a team norm, not a private trick.

### Polishing is procrastination

If an edit to a rules file didn't change what someone can or can't do, it wasn't a real edit.

### Define done, or nothing stops

This applies to people and tools equally. "Improve the footer" has no terminal state.

---

## 4. Working with AI tooling

*New section. The expensive failures on this project were not bad code — they were unrequested
work and unrequested commits.*

### The authorisation ladder — three separate levels

**Investigate ≠ fix ≠ commit.** "Run it" and "have a look" are investigation requests. They are
not approval to change code, and changing code is not approval to commit it.

Correct shape: **change → verify → stop and show the diff → wait.**

This sharpens AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15 with the distinction the rule leaves implicit. Resuming
from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is **not** an instruction to
commit.

### The audit-loop failure mode

A build can become a self-sustaining audit-and-fix cycle that feels productive and isn't.
Measured on one stretch of SFCC-55: **55 commits, a 3.0:1 rework ratio, `footer/index.tsx`
touched 32 times in 5 days.** The work wasn't wasted — it was mis-ordered.

**The diagnostic that separates real work from generated work:** where did the finding come
from? Six findings fixed things that were actually broken. Seven came from *reading code we'd
just written*. If a finding's origin is your own fresh output rather than a spec, a reproduced
failure, or a review comment, it is probably not the next thing to do.

Two correctives:

- **Read the review queue before starting a self-directed pass.** A six-hour-old Major finding
  named a live security bypass while the loop was polishing comment placement.
- **Ban "it's good practice" as a justification.** A fix needs a named requirement, a
  reproduced failure, or a review comment behind it.

### Present verdicts, don't auto-fix

When a pass produces a list of possible improvements, separate the ones traceable to a
spec/failure/review from the ones traceable to your own just-written code — and **offer** the
second group rather than doing them.

### Don't take an agent's report at face value

Two agent claims were overturned by direct verification in a single session this week: that
a11y is ungated (it is gated — the agent was reasoning from Storybook 8), and that the CLI
would work with the repo's management token (it reads neither that env var nor any other).

Both were confidently stated and internally coherent. **The check is cheap; the propagation
cost is not** — a wrong claim in a doc gets cited for months.

### Local-only docs stay local

These three files live on this machine. **Never cite them in a PR reply, a commit message, or
a code comment.** A citation nobody else can open reads as an appeal to a private authority,
and for CodeRabbit specifically it teaches the bot nothing.

When a local doc is the real reason for a decision, find the public equivalent in `AGENTS.md`,
`.claude/rules/` or `.docs/` and cite that. If none exists, argue the merits directly.

No `Co-Authored-By` trailer on commits.

---

## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

*Covers responsibilities 5, 16*

Four rungs: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and
needs justification.

**Where to look:** `.claude/registry/` for `Origin` (`Custom` / `Override` / **`Base`**), then
`ui-kits/`. ⚠️ The registry's `Tier` column is unreliable — `generateRegistry.mjs:122`
hardcodes tiers, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything to Tier 4.

**`Origin = Base` is the hidden cost.** It means copy-first: mirror the file, convert to TS,
verify the override renders, *then* build. That's real effort and it belongs in the estimate.
Eight components referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` are still base.

**The `shared/ui` barrel exception.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate styling into
base cart/checkout/account looks like enormous leverage. It intercepts nothing — the barrel
re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite, and 208 base files import the barrel
while 0 import the individual module. Don't scope a story around it.

**Duplicate atoms are a human problem.** No tool detects "this is a second Button." The fix
that makes it self-service is one line in the BA's story template: *name the component, and
state whether it exists.*

### The atoms governance model — decided

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
```

Tier by composition (what the component's own template renders), camelCase for
Zimmermann-authored, a registered recipe always.

⚠️ **The rules set is split on this.** `components.md` and `conventions.md` contain **zero**
occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29`
still scaffolds to the flat path. `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself. Reconciling this
is a standing item.

---

## Play 2 — Estimation validation

*Covers responsibilities 2, 6*

**The re-baseline to say once:** pages go *down*, components go *up by more*. Component-based
decomposition front-loads the work.

Split component-build effort from page-composition effort in every estimate. They have
different risk profiles and different owners.

Challenge list:

1. Is it `Origin = Base`? Add copy-first.
2. Does it exist in `ui-kits` already?
3. Is a Contentful content type needed? That's a second story.
4. Is the Figma frame signed off, or "Not Confirmed"?
5. Does it depend on an integration that isn't wired? Most aren't.
6. Does its data exist on the tiers it must demo on?
7. Is it multi-site? Eight storefronts, eleven locales, by default.

---

## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review

*Covers responsibilities 3, 9*

**Configuration variant** (a prop) vs **composition variant** (a container or slot —
structurally a second component). Getting this wrong at story time produces a component that
can't express what the design needs.

⚠️ **Contentful sync is additive-only**, so a variant modelled wrongly is semi-permanent. Field
deletion is opt-in (`--delete-deleted-fields`) and off by default, deliberately.

Optional fields need explicit AC for the absent case — see the three-tier absent-data policy in
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7.

---

## Play 4 — The renderer contract

*Covers responsibilities 4, 12*

One field-ID table, **identical in both stories** of a Contentful pair. You own the template,
the BA fills it, you sign off the field IDs.

# FED Lead Playbook

**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026

The lead role: what you say, to whom, and when. Judgement and process, not procedure.

**Companions:** `fedBuild-manual.md` (how to build a component) · `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why
the machine behaves the way it does).

**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this file disagrees with it,
that file wins.

*This document absorbed `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (retired 25 Aug 2026). Its
durable operating principles are §3; its training-vehicle material — a Next.js/Tailwind stack
that isn't this one — was dropped.*

---

## 1. The mandate

Sixteen responsibilities landed across two Contentful-vs-PWA-Kit alignment meetings. They
reduce to two mandates:

- **M1 — Protect the build.** Reuse, conventions, review, accessibility, performance.
- **M2 — Protect the plan.** Estimation, scope, dependencies, escalation.

**The one to resist as stated:** being a serial refinement gate across both squads. It won't
scale and it will slip. Name that rather than absorbing it — an unresourced ask that quietly
becomes yours is the failure mode here.

### The quality bar this serves

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3**, for the whole project. Three consequences:

1. **Vigilance is the job**, not an overhead on it.
2. **Budget real time per UI PR** — an hour or more. That's the cost of the review, not
   slippage.
3. **Flag rather than invent.** A guessed value that ships is a defect with your name on it.

---

## 2. Operating rhythm

| Moment | Plays |
|---|---|
| Story drafting | 1, 3, 4 |
| Refinement | 1, 2, 8 |
| Pre-sprint planning | 2, 8 |
| PR review | 5, 5b, 6 |
| Weekly design review | 9 |

---

## 3. Principles

*Absorbed from the retired playbook. These are the parts that survived contact with the
codebase.*

### The quality ceiling is set by the human

An AI assistant has no standards of its own — the standards and the constraints are things you
supply. Its real value is making your assumptions visible faster, not making decisions.

### The dual mandate

You hold two hats and the failure mode is collapsing into one.

| | IC | Lead |
|---|---|---|
| Think | about the component | about the system |
| Ask | until the spec is unambiguous | until the *team's* spec is unambiguous |
| Decide | how to build it | whether it should be built now |
| Review | your own output hardest | the pattern, not the line |
| Protect | the build | the plan |
| Multiply | — | the highest-leverage thing you do |

**IC drift:** you're the only one who knows how something works. **Lead drift:** you haven't
written code in a week and your review comments are getting vaguer.

### Defeating agreeableness

An assistant that agrees with you is worth nothing. Four techniques that work:

- **Role framing** — "you are a reviewer whose job is to find what's wrong with this."
- **Steelman** — "give me the strongest argument *against* this approach."
- **Critique-first** — ask for the problems before asking for the solution.
- **Constraint injection** — name the constraint it must satisfy, so it can't hand-wave.

Make it a team norm, not a private trick.

### Polishing is procrastination

If an edit to a rules file didn't change what someone can or can't do, it wasn't a real edit.

### Define done, or nothing stops

This applies to people and tools equally. "Improve the footer" has no terminal state.

---

## 4. Working with AI tooling

*New section. The expensive failures on this project were not bad code — they were unrequested
work and unrequested commits.*

### The authorisation ladder — three separate levels

**Investigate ≠ fix ≠ commit.** "Run it" and "have a look" are investigation requests. They are
not approval to change code, and changing code is not approval to commit it.

Correct shape: **change → verify → stop and show the diff → wait.**

This sharpens AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15 with the distinction the rule leaves implicit. Resuming
from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is **not** an instruction to
commit.

### The audit-loop failure mode

A build can become a self-sustaining audit-and-fix cycle that feels productive and isn't.
Measured on one stretch of SFCC-55: **55 commits, a 3.0:1 rework ratio, `footer/index.tsx`
touched 32 times in 5 days.** The work wasn't wasted — it was mis-ordered.

**The diagnostic that separates real work from generated work:** where did the finding come
from? Six findings fixed things that were actually broken. Seven came from *reading code we'd
just written*. If a finding's origin is your own fresh output rather than a spec, a reproduced
failure, or a review comment, it is probably not the next thing to do.

Two correctives:

- **Read the review queue before starting a self-directed pass.** A six-hour-old Major finding
  named a live security bypass while the loop was polishing comment placement.
- **Ban "it's good practice" as a justification.** A fix needs a named requirement, a
  reproduced failure, or a review comment behind it.

### Present verdicts, don't auto-fix

When a pass produces a list of possible improvements, separate the ones traceable to a
spec/failure/review from the ones traceable to your own just-written code — and **offer** the
second group rather than doing them.

### Don't take an agent's report at face value

Two agent claims were overturned by direct verification in a single session this week: that
a11y is ungated (it is gated — the agent was reasoning from Storybook 8), and that the CLI
would work with the repo's management token (it reads neither that env var nor any other).

Both were confidently stated and internally coherent. **The check is cheap; the propagation
cost is not** — a wrong claim in a doc gets cited for months.

### Local-only docs stay local

These three files live on this machine. **Never cite them in a PR reply, a commit message, or
a code comment.** A citation nobody else can open reads as an appeal to a private authority,
and for CodeRabbit specifically it teaches the bot nothing.

When a local doc is the real reason for a decision, find the public equivalent in `AGENTS.md`,
`.claude/rules/` or `.docs/` and cite that. If none exists, argue the merits directly.

No `Co-Authored-By` trailer on commits.

---

## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

*Covers responsibilities 5, 16*

Four rungs: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and
needs justification.

**Where to look:** `.claude/registry/` for `Origin` (`Custom` / `Override` / **`Base`**), then
`ui-kits/`. ⚠️ The registry's `Tier` column is unreliable — `generateRegistry.mjs:122`
hardcodes tiers, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything to Tier 4.

**`Origin = Base` is the hidden cost.** It means copy-first: mirror the file, convert to TS,
verify the override renders, *then* build. That's real effort and it belongs in the estimate.
Eight components referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` are still base.

**The `shared/ui` barrel exception.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate styling into
base cart/checkout/account looks like enormous leverage. It intercepts nothing — the barrel
re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite, and 208 base files import the barrel
while 0 import the individual module. Don't scope a story around it.

**Duplicate atoms are a human problem.** No tool detects "this is a second Button." The fix
that makes it self-service is one line in the BA's story template: *name the component, and
state whether it exists.*

### The atoms governance model — decided

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
```

Tier by composition (what the component's own template renders), camelCase for
Zimmermann-authored, a registered recipe always.

⚠️ **The rules set is split on this.** `components.md` and `conventions.md` contain **zero**
occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29`
still scaffolds to the flat path. `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself. Reconciling this
is a standing item.

---

## Play 2 — Estimation validation

*Covers responsibilities 2, 6*

**The re-baseline to say once:** pages go *down*, components go *up by more*. Component-based
decomposition front-loads the work.

Split component-build effort from page-composition effort in every estimate. They have
different risk profiles and different owners.

Challenge list:

1. Is it `Origin = Base`? Add copy-first.
2. Does it exist in `ui-kits` already?
3. Is a Contentful content type needed? That's a second story.
4. Is the Figma frame signed off, or "Not Confirmed"?
5. Does it depend on an integration that isn't wired? Most aren't.
6. Does its data exist on the tiers it must demo on?
7. Is it multi-site? Eight storefronts, eleven locales, by default.

---

## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review

*Covers responsibilities 3, 9*

**Configuration variant** (a prop) vs **composition variant** (a container or slot —
structurally a second component). Getting this wrong at story time produces a component that
can't express what the design needs.

⚠️ **Contentful sync is additive-only**, so a variant modelled wrongly is semi-permanent. Field
deletion is opt-in (`--delete-deleted-fields`) and off by default, deliberately.

Optional fields need explicit AC for the absent case — see the three-tier absent-data policy in
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7.

---

## Play 4 — The renderer contract

*Covers responsibilities 4, 12*

One field-ID table, **identical in both stories** of a Contentful pair. You own the template,
the BA fills it, you sign off the field IDs.

The IDs are the contract. A rename after authoring begins is a migration, not an edit.

---
